News.title: Reward offered over murder in flat used as brothel
News.content:
A Â£20,000 reward is being offered by Crimestoppers in connection with the murder of a man who was found dead in a Birmingham flat in 2022.

Jinming Zhang had been stabbed multiple times before he was found in the property, which police said was being used as a brothel, in Moseley Street in Digbeth.

West Midlands Police previously released CCTV of a suspect, while a DNA sample from the suspected killer found at the scene did not produce a match on the national database.

The case was featured in the BBC series of Forensics: The Real CSI last year, which revealed police believed the murder suspect may have sustained a hand injury in the frenzied attack.

Jenny Birch, who has been overseeing the investigation, urged anyone with information "no matter how small" to contact police.

"Someone out there knows something, and we won't give up until we have answers," she said.

News.title: Sam Fender calls out ticket prices ahead of tour
News.content:
Sam Fender has said he has removed a ticket category from sale after being unhappy with pricing for his upcoming tour.

The 32-year-old announced his Proper Massive Stadium Tour earlier this week, which will visit Newcastle, Cardiff, London, Edinburgh, Dublin and Manchester in summer 2027.

While tickets are yet to go on sale, Fender responded to a post on social media which claimed to outline the expected ticket prices.

The Geordie musician now appears to have lowered the prices and said the "costs are astronomical compared to two years ago" but he could not control the venue or ticketing fees.

Tickets are due to go on general sale at 09:30 GMT on Friday, with a pre-sale at the same time on Wednesday.

Fender initially said he was "not happy" with the reported prices.

"They're getting changed," he said on Instagram.

"It got inflated well more than I'd had in mind, it should only be inflated in relation to the cost of putting the show on."

News.title: Table for 1? Nearly 40 percent of all restaurant visits are solo diners
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Nearly 40 percent of all restaurant visits are now from solo diners as society becomes more comfortable with doing things alone, a new analysis has found.

With dating apps drying up and friends being too busy to do anything other than sending memes back and forth, people are embracing the idea of taking themselves out on a date — whether that be to a restaurant, a coffee shop or even a concert.

“It’s hard for me to want a boyfriend because I take myself on cute solo dates,” New York City-based influencer Anna Barger said in a video back in 2023.

Since then, the trend has only grown.

About 38 percent of restaurant visits are solo occasions this year, Restaurant Business reported, citing data from foodservice research platform Technomic Ignite. This is up from roughly 30 percent in 2019.

open image in gallery Nearly 40 percent of all restaurant visits are now from solo diners as society becomes more comfortable with doing things alone ( Getty Images )

While someone enjoying a quick alone meal at a fast-food restaurant during their lunch break and it isn’t considered out of the ordinary, there’s also a growing number of people pulling up to a white-tablecloth dinner solo.

Nearly 22 percent of visits to fine dining restaurants have been from solo guests this year, up from less than 10 percent in 2019.

One TikToker based in Toronto filmed herself eating a meal at a restaurant and told viewers, “If you ever see me eating alone at a restaurant, please don’t feel bad for me — ‘cause I am having the best time of my life.”

She captioned the October 8 video, “Table for one, happiness for two.”

open image in gallery Dining alone has not just boomed post-COVID, but has been becoming more popular over the past two decades ( Getty Images )

“People are receptive to the idea that I can go to the restaurant, sit down, maybe watch what’s on the TV or whatever and do my thing and just scroll through my phone and be alone at the restaurant and get that experience of being served,” Robert Byrne, senior director of consumer research with Technomic, told Restaurant Business.

Dining alone has not just boomed post-COVID, but has been becoming more popular over the past two decades.

In 2003, just around 17 percent of Americans said they ate all their meals alone the previous day, according to the 2025 World Happiness Report.

The number of Americans eating all their daily meals alone increased to roughly 26 percent by 2023.

News.title: British Airways plane encounters drone ‘the size of four toasters’ after Heathrow take-off
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A British Airways plane encountered a drone “the size of four toasters” after taking-off from Heathrow Airport, air safety officials have revealed.

The New York City-bound flight had only recently departed London Heathrow Airport on June 24 when it encountered the drone.

The pilot told Air Traffic Control that a drone had flown in the opposite direction about 50 feet above the plane’s right wing at 12.08pm.

The plane didn’t have to take any action to avoid the drone, a British Airways spokesman said.

The drone flew straight past the aircraft and the Boeing 777 arrived at its destination as planned.

A drone flew past a British Airways plane the “size of four toasters”, air safety officials revealed ( PA Wire )

The UK Aiprox Board said in its monthly report of close encounters that the plane was 6,000ft in the air when the “shiny, silver object” whizzed past.

“They said it was moving very fast, was probably of silver colour, metallic and reflective,” the report said.

“After an enquiry as to its size, the [pilot] reported to them that it was about the ‘size of four toasters’.”

A spokesperson for British Airways said: “We take matters such as these extremely seriously, and our pilots report these incidents so authorities can investigate them and take appropriate action.”

News.title: Is Barcelona v Real Madrid on TV? How to watch El Clasico in the UK
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Barcelona and Real Madrid resume their bitter rivalry with the first El Clasico of this LaLiga campaign.

Hansi Flick’s side have the upper hand in the top flight so far, with a perfect run of nine wins from nine, while Jose Mourinho’s visitors sit third, six points off top spot having won seven and lost two.

Barca ran out 5-2 winners in an entertaining clash with 10-man Real Betis last time out, with Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Dani Olmo all on the scoresheet, while Kylian Mbappe scored twice as Real beat Sevilla 4-1.

Whatever happens it is likely to be a dramatic, all-out-attacking game: Barcelona lost 4-2 to holders PSG in a Champions League thriller on Tuesday while Madrid put four past RB Leipzig, who scored a late consolation goal, on Wednesday night.

Here’s everything you need to know.

When is Barcelona v Real Madrid?

Barcelona host Real Madrid at Camp Nou on Sunday 25 October, with kick-off at 8pm BST.

How can I watch it?

Viewers in the UK can watch the game on Premier Sports 1.

Team news

Barcelona’s Dani Olmo picked up an injury in the defeat to PSG and joins Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde on the sidelines.

Real Madrid will be without the suspended Vinicius Jr after he was sent off against Villareal and handed a four-game ban for violent conduct following a hair-pull on Nathan Saliba. The visitors will also be missing injured defender Raul Asencio.

News.title: Architect struck off after bizarre neighbour dispute over 'phallic symbol' car
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A Norwich architect who accused a neighbour of gender violence by using his car as a “phallic symbol” on her driveway has been struck off for making unfounded claims against her neighbours.

Dr Karin Elliott was removed from the register for at least two years by the Architects Registration Board after sending inappropriate communications that amounted to unacceptable professional conduct.

A tribunal decided that she used “inflammatory language, making a series of misleading and potentially damaging accusations” in 2024 regarding her neighbours, “with scant regard to their accuracy”.

The board described the Irish-American architect’s actions as “misleading, lacking integrity and dishonest”.

Ms Elliott accused one neighbour of “racial harassment” through false claims that he wielded a chainsaw in her garden, the tribunal heard.

The architect’s partner, Francois Girardin, told the tribunal that none of the neighbours said “anything directly racist”.

open image in gallery Dr Elliott’s partner claimed that their neighbours would ‘cheer for England’ whenever the country played France ( Getty )

However, Mr Girardin, who is French, made an “inference” of racism from how “sometimes a Union Jack would appear” and “a wall had been constructed after the US president had talked about building a big wall to keep out immigrants”, the tribunal heard.

Mr Girardin also said whenever England played sport, a neighbour would “leave their doors open, and – especially when England played France – their family would cheer for England”.

During cross-examination, Dr Elliott said from “a psychoanalytic perspective” her neighbour repeatedly driving across her driveway with the “phallic symbol” of his car was a manifestation of gender violence.

The tribunal found this “underscored how tenuously she constructed serious accusations against other people, and how casually she dispensed them”.

The architect had made a planning application for the installation of CCTV cameras on her property in December 2023, following disputes with her neighbours.

She wrote a letter to local residents in February 2024 asking for support with the application, and made serious allegations about her neighbours that the tribunal considered to be “dishonest” and “misleading”.

In the letter, she claimed one neighbour had “smashed down several of our historic walls, chopped down many of our historic trees, and built on our property, all without our consent”.

Discussing another neighbour, Dr Elliott wrote: “He calls us either a ‘piece of s***’, ‘disgusting’ and/or exclaims ‘the stench’ regularly.”

In another allegation, the architect wrote: “He threatened to hit one of us over the head with a hammer at one stage, after he was asked to desist.

“He had been starting to build a wall on our property illegally on a Sunday, following Trump’s declaration that he would ‘build a big wall’ to keep out immigrants.

“It is very upsetting. We are Irish/American and French.”

open image in gallery Part of a border wall between the US and Mexico ( Getty )

Discussing claims about a third neighbour, Dr Elliott accused her of building an “ugly concrete foundation” and using influence at the local council “to escape justice”.

She also accused her neighbour of singing “Tragedy” by the Bee Gees “from the enormous balcony they built overlooking our home” after the death of her father.

Discussing the three neighbours, Dr Elliott wrote: “We hope that the CCTV might deter them all from further trespassing and further destroying our listed garden, and from any further gender violence and racial harassment.”

In cross-examination, the architect said: “I think I’d give this letter a serious editing if I did it again.”

Dr Elliott made further allegations in a planning appeal form to the Norwich City Planning Portal in March 2024.

Discussing one neighbour in the planning form, she wrote: “I begged him to turn off his chainsaw and explained that I considered it to be racial harassment.”

One neighbour told the tribunal that the architect’s “bizarre accusations of threatening behaviour and the racist accusations have been a source of acute embarrassment and personal discomfort”.

Another said the allegations were “very depressing and upsetting” and they do not spend time in their garden because Ms Elliott and her partner are “always looking at us”, adding that the architect is an “absolute disgrace to her profession”.

The tribunal found that Dr Elliott’s conduct occurred after she had previously been found guilty of unacceptable professional conduct in 2021 for calling neighbours “racists and Nazis”, as well as “making offensive references to their physical characteristics and mental health”.

News.title: New York Catholic Archdiocese to pay $800 million in historic abuse settlement
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Archdiocese of New York has agreed to an $800 million settlement with approximately 1,300 victims of clergy sexual abuse, marking the second-largest payout by a U.S. Catholic archdiocese.

Archbishop Ronald Hicks sent an email Saturday to clergy confirming the settlement after attorneys for the survivors of alleged abuse announced it. Hicks said the agreement will not be final until the parties sign it, an action scheduled for the week of Nov. 6.

The Archdiocese of Los Angeles reached the largest U.S. sexual abuse settlement to date, agreeing in 2024 to pay $880 million to 1,000 victims in addition to $740 million in previous payouts.

Other major Catholic archdiocese settlements include $395 million in San Francisco for around 500 lawsuits and at least $230 million approved in New Orleans.

The agreement with the New York archdiocese would end more than seven years of lawsuits. The parties agreed to a framework for an agreement in May that required everyone who filed a claim to sign off.

New York Archdiocese Abuse Settlement ( AP )

“The unanimous agreement of survivors who filed claims against the Archdiocese of New York marks a powerful moment in the pursuit of justice,” Jeff Anderson, an attorney representing people who filed more than 1,000 of claims against the Catholic Church in New York state, said in a statement.

“Through their courage, sacrifice, and determination, survivors have helped bring about a reckoning and a meaningful step toward accountability.”

The Archdiocese of New York covers the city's boroughs of the Bronx, Manhattan and Staten Island as well as seven counties to the north of New York City and is home to about 300 churches, more than 150 parochial schools and 2.5 million Catholics.

In his email to clergy, Hicks said that if church members ask about the settlement, “please let them know that much progress has been made.”

“We are on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors,” he wrote. “This agreement will also allow the archdiocese to turn its full attention once again to its mission of preaching the Gospel, healing the sick, caring for the poor and needy, welcoming the stranger, and educating our children.”

A New York law enacted in 2019 allows survivors of child sexual abuse to file lawsuits against their abusers and institutions that shielded them until they turn 55. People who had already had turned 55 when the law was enacted also were given until August 2021 to file lawsuits, no matter when the alleged abuse occurred.

“This is an extraordinary achievement for the survivors,” said Trusha Goffe, an attorney in Anderson’s firm. "The survivors remined resolute through years of litigation to reach this monumental settlement.”

News.title: Brendon McCullum convinced England can learn from agonising defeat to Pakistan
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Brendon McCullum has vowed England will learn from yet another agonising loss which has left their bid to make next weekend’s tri-series final hanging in the balance.

Three days after Sri Lanka chased a staggering 430 in Rawalpindi, England looked set to break their duck in the tournament when they reduced Pakistan to 154 for nine in their pursuit of 242 in Lahore.

Shadab Khan had other ideas, though, as his maiden international hundred with just number 11 batter Haris Rauf for support sealed an unlikely one-wicket victory and a third defeat in a row for England.

open image in gallery Shadab Khan celebrates his century (K.M. Chaudary/PA) ( AP )

Harry Brook’s side are now all but eliminated from the tri-series and their exit will be confirmed on Tuesday if Pakistan get beaten by Sri Lanka, who then face England on Thursday in the final group game.

McCullum admitted the past few days have been bruising for his team but, with the 50-over World Cup in southern Africa in 12 months’ time in mind, he believes this has been a worthwhile experience.

“We will learn from this,” England’s white-ball head coach said. “The boys are gutted, to be honest. They were gutted after the last game and they’re even more gutted after this one.

“These boys are immensely talented, they’re incredibly driven to perform for England, we know that we’re not the best side that we can be just yet but that’s the challenge that’s in front of us.

open image in gallery Brendon McCullum is keen to build towards the World Cup (John Walton/PA) ( PA Wire )

“There’s some good lessons and learning opportunities and we will learn from it because we are desperate to get to South Africa and have a realistic chance of challenging for that World Cup.”

Shadab’s 113 not out is the highest score by a number eight in ODIs and he impeccably marshalled the chase as Rauf faced just 19 balls in an unbroken last-wicket stand of 89 off 80 deliveries.

It meant that Ben Duckett’s 105 in England’s 241 all out – a total that looked below-par only for a collective effort from their bowlers to take them to the brink of victory – was in a losing cause.

open image in gallery Ben Duckett’s ton was in vain (K.M. Chaudary/PA) ( AP )

Asked what they could have differently, McCullum replied: “It’s so fresh. We’ll look at it in the next little while, go through all the footage, the data and analytics and look at some of the options if we’re placed in that situation another time.

“They are the conversations we are having and we need to keep having. When you’ve got an inexperienced line-up and you’ve got a big World Cup in 12 months’ time and you’ve only got 20 games between now and then, you need to have that level of communication and those examples of real time experiences.”

Shadab was given out lbw to Gus Atkinson on 97 and the teams were even shaking hands, only for a hopeful review to show the all-rounder had grazed the ball with his bat.

There was more drama when the umpire failed to signal a wide from Sam Curran’s final ball of an over, prompting Rauf and Will Jacks into a confrontation as tensions rose.

open image in gallery Tensions rose between Will Jacks and Haris Rauf (Mike Egerton/PA) ( PA Wire )

Joe Root had to separate former Yorkshire team-mate Rauf from Jacks and it was the tail-end batter who had the last laugh as Pakistan, clad in pink to raise awareness for breast cancer, sealed victory with a four to leave England feeling blue.

Assessing the coming together between Rauf and Jacks, McCullum said: “It’s just cricket. Teams are playing for their country and it means a lot.

“There are pressure situations and moments where we get a little bit confrontational but it’s just the way it is. There’s no malice in it. I know Haris very well, he’s a good competitor and so is Will Jacks, and you’d expect nothing else from that.”

News.title: England suffer astonishing defeat by Pakistan after Shadab’s remarkable reprieve
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, over-by-over coverage of Pakistan v England in Lahore. In the UK, the clocks went back an hour overnight; England would love to wind them back 72 hours and have another go at defending 429 against Sri Lanka. That unfathomable defeat in Rawalpindi has left them on the brink in this tri-series.

England won’t be mathematically eliminated if they lose to Pakistan today, but it would leave them needing snookers if they are to reach Saturday’s final. Realistically, they need to win the last two group games, and there’s a chance even that might not be enough.

“It’s my first tri-series and it replicates World Cup styles and pressures,” said the England all-rounder Will Jacks. “You can’t replicate that in training or a bilateral series. In World Cups you have to bounce back. I remember in 2019 when England lost a couple of games in the group and they had to win their last two and they were able to do that to take the momentum forward.

“I’m not saying it’s the same thing but it’s a mini version of that and hopefully we can win on Sunday and move on. We have the opportunity to play in two must-win fixtures. Sometimes you learn more in losses than you do in wins.”

Jacks’ Surrey team-mate Sam Curran suffered the most against Sri Lanka, conceding an eye-watering 103 from his nine overs.

“They were incredibly hard conditions to bowl in and he bowls a lot of pressure overs – that’s his role in the team,” said Jacks. “He’s been so successful with that for England over a number of years. There are some days where it doesn’t quite work.”

Curran has kept his place in the side – but Josh Tongue is replaced by Henry Crocombe, who makes his international debut. And there’s no recall for Adil Rashid. We’ll have the toss and full team news in a moment.

News.title: Iraola era taking shape as Liverpool see off high-flying Brighton
News.content:
A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish; Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak have probably been doing it repeatedly in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, they combined for a niche moment in Liverpool’s history.

Anfield has never seen a more expensively created goal but, at a combined cost of £248m, Barcola and Isak had a little landmark. What was more important, however, were the three points it led to and now Andoni Iraola’s reign is starting to take shape.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against a high-flying, well-respected team in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0.

But Liverpool, inspired by their expensive recruits, rose to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

News.title: Hapless and hopeless Man Utd bring curtain down on out-of-depth Carrick
News.content:
Hapless, hopeless and utterly humiliated. And that has to be that for Michael Carrick. It is surely inconceivable that he will continue any longer as Manchester United’s head coach. A proud club on its knees and a favoured son on his way out.

The former midfielder will carry the can. As managers always do. Even if the fault lines run so deep at United it feels like they are almost irreparable. Owners – the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – executives, players. A collective failing of monumental proportions. Although, again, it will be the manager who goes. Carrick knows it and looked like he knows it. He knows the score, especially after this score.

More than four years ago Ralf Rangnick, the then-interim manager, declared that United needed “open heart surgery”. Now there is barely a pulse.

An announcement must be imminent with United turning to someone else in the fight against Premier League relegation. A joke? No, this abject performance against Bournemouth leaves United in 16th place, just a point above the bottom three, so the priority for the new man will be clear. Save them from the drop. They are 14 points off the top already but forget that. It is an irrelevance given their plight.

News.title: Antonelli takes another step closer to F1 title with US GP pole position
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas, just outside of Austin. This is one of the finest tracks that we have on the Formula One calendar and is a fitting place for the US Grand Prix. The races are usually entertaining, the drivers love the track (though have complained about the bumps this year) and it comfortably the best on-track action of the three races in the US.

What might we see this weekend? Well, Kimi Antonelli could be crowned world champion if results go his way. The way the results need to go make that fairly unlikely, but stranger things have happened in F1 and they often do. In any case, it would take a catastrophic implosion for Antonelli to lose the championship from here, so it is a case of when rather than if.

Who looks in good form? Well, Ferrari do. They have brought an updated car here this weekend it, so far, is paying off. Charles Leclerc had good pace yesterday and Lewis Hamilton, his team-mate, was fastest earlier today in final practice. Hamilton’s time of 1min34.893sec was a tenth or two quicker than the Red Bull of Max Verstappen, with Leclerc not too far behind. Then it was Antonelli, George Russell in the second Mercedes and Oscar Piastri making up the top six, though the Australian was nearly half a second off the ultimate pace of Hamilton.

Qualifying begins in about 50 minutes and we will be here with all the updates from that.

News.title: Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head
News.content:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

“I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso said. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

“We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”

News.title: Pollock at heart of scuffle that inspires Leicester to thumping win in feisty derby
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

News.title: Saliba has fight on his hands to usurp ‘unbelievable’ Konsa
News.content:
Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta said: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

“I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes said: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

News.title: ‘Tactical genius’ Emery outsmarts Maresca as City crash to first league defeat
News.content:
It was four years ago to the day that Emery grabbed this famous club by the shirt and collar and gave them an almighty shake. After a summer of much instability including many player sales, he appears to have already struck a formula with his newly assembled team.

There were a number of fine individual performances from many of the summer arrivals, such as Jackson, goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and Johan Manzambi.

Emery said: “We were very motivated and Manchester City is the best team in the world so this is the level. This year we started so poorly and we needed time to understand how we improve. The players showed the capacity to retrieve the level we’ve had over the last few years.

“Nicolas is more mature and very demanding of himself to improve. Earlier this season he was shooting over the crossbar but he is now finding the corners. There is still work to do and 11 points is not enough but we are feeling better.”

Villa were fierce from the start and ahead after six minutes. Guéhi’s mistake was punished by John McGinn, with the ball dropping to Jackson who crashed a shot into the roof of the net.

The home team did require Suzuki to produce saves to stop efforts from Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov as City responded. Ndiaye also struck the outside of the post and City were level seven minutes into the second half with Erling Haaland nodding in Ndiaye’s cross at the far post. Haaland had touched the ball just eight times in the opening 45 minutes but invariably only needs one chance.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick admits ‘there’s no hiding from it’ as he risks sack after Man Utd’s woeful defeat to Bournemouth
Sports.content:

MICHAEL CARRICK has admitted he does not know what comes next as his Manchester United future hangs in the balance.

The under-fire boss was left reeling after United were taken apart for the second time in a week, with Bournemouth running out 3-0 winners at Old Trafford for the third time in four seasons.



Carrick, 45, offered little reassurance over his position when speaking to Sky Sports after the final whistle.

He told Sky Sports: “It’s a tough situation. There’s no hiding from it. What it looks like, what’s next, I really don’t know.



“I always do what’s best for this football club. I’ve said it all along and I don’t change that now.

“I love what I do. I love the position I’m in. I feel the responsibility.”



The defeat followed Wednesday’s humiliating 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas‘ Como, piling further pressure on a manager who had enjoyed a promising spell in charge in the second half of last season.

Today, United were rocked by goals from Rayan and Marcus Tavernier before half-time, leaving the hosts with a mountain to climb.

Evanilson then struck in the second half to compound the misery and leave Carrick facing fresh questions over his team’s direction.

The manager admitted his players had been hurting after another damaging afternoon.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He said: “It was a tough day for them. We went into the game being rocked a bit, and you could feel that on the pitch. But we kept going until the end.

“We are disappointed and hurt in there. The players, or the ones I have spoken to, are feeling it.”

Carrick also acknowledged the difficult circumstances surrounding his team, with injuries and selection decisions adding to the challenge.

Asked about the hand of cards he had been dealt, including the recent comments made by Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes, he said: “It’s really difficult for me to have a day like this at this football club, to feel this emotion and dynamics of what it felt like – not for me personally, but for Man Utd.

“It was really mixed today, and I feel a lot of responsibility. It hurts a lot seeing us go through like this at this moment in time.



“There’s always times in games where you’re trying to make decisions to try and change the course of play. They were decisions we made today.”

The comments come after a turbulent couple of weeks behind the scenes at Old Trafford.

Martinez questioned the club’s hierarchy following the 2-0 defeat away to Atletico Madrid, and a week later Fernandes raised concerns over Carrick’s tactics after the Como thrashing.



The United captain was then left on the bench for the whole of today’s game, despite his side chasing a way back into the contest.

It is a dramatic reversal of fortunes for Carrick, who earned widespread praise after collecting 39 points during the second half of last season while serving as interim boss.

He stepped into the role after Ruben Amorim‘s departure in January and appeared to give United fresh momentum.

But doubts have grown over the club’s summer business and whether the squad has enough quality and balance to sustain that progress.

Carrick was also asked about the mood among the supporters, who repeatedly sang his name despite growing frustration after another poor performance.



He said: “It wasn’t from me. It was really mixed emotions. I’m really feeling it for my players, and the boys are feeling it at the moment.

“It’s mixed emotions to feel what I felt from the supporters. I really felt their support, but we haven’t had the results and the performances haven’t been good enough.”

The former midfielder is one of seven permanent managers to have taken charge of United since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013 — a figure that rises to ten if interim bosses are included.

Now, with the club’s season threatening to unravel, speculation is mounting over who could replace him if the hierarchy decides to make another change.

Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are among the names being mentioned as potential candidates.

Sports.title: Bizarre moment Liverpool star makes slide tackle with his HEAD as fans hail unrivalled commitment
Sports.content:
Next

LIVERPOOL fans have hailed Ronald Araujo’s unrivalled commitment after the defender produced a bizarre slide tackle using his HEAD.

The Uruguayan threw himself into a desperate challenge on Brighton’s Maxim De Cuyper following a scramble around the visitors’ box.



Rather than sticking out a leg, Araujo appeared to launch his head towards the ball to make the crucial clearance whilst lying on the ground.

Ryan Gravenberch then seized upon the loose ball and helped Liverpool bring the danger to an end.



The remarkable moment left fans stunned, with supporters praising the defender’s willingness to put his body on the line.

One fan wrote on Reddit: “The sort of s*** that really makes the fans fall in love with you.”



Another added: “Whatever Iraola’s been doing with him in practice, it’s working.”

A third Liverpool supporter simply declared: “I love this man.”

Araujo’s heroic defending helped Liverpool preserve their 2-0 lead as they secured a fourth consecutive win in all competitions.

A Pascal Gross own goal and Alexander Isak‘s first-half strike proved enough to seal the victory and lift Liverpool into fourth place.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

They now sit just one point behind third-placed Brighton, who are five points adrift of the top two, Manchester City and Arsenal, on 21 points.

The tackle also brought back memories of another unforgettable Premier League moment involving Phil Jones.

In May 2015, the former Manchester United defender famously went to ground and used his head to challenge Arsenal’s Olivier Giroud in a desperate attempt to win the ball.

Araujo, 26, joined Liverpool from Barcelona on loan with an option to buy next summer for around £47million.



He arrived on Merseyside after falling out of favour as a first-choice centre-back under Barcelona boss Hansi Flick, despite previously serving as the Catalan club’s captain.

Araujo is currently operating at right-back for Liverpool, with Jeremy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk occupying the central defensive positions.

The move appears to be giving him a chance to rediscover his best form.

His standout campaign came in the 2022/23 season under Xavi, when Barcelona kept 17 clean sheets in the 22 La Liga matches he played and conceded just five goals with him on the pitch.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace 0 Newcastle 2: Pierre Sage in huge trouble at Selhurst Park as Toon bounce back from consecutive defeats
Sports.content:
Next

HARVEY BARNES sealed Newcastle a vital win in the capital to heap more pressure on under-fire Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage.

The hosts failed to convert a number of first-half chances against what had been an awful opening 45 minutes from the Geordies.



But William Osula stunned Selhurst Park by firing the Toon in front two minutes after the break before Barnes struck a second 11 minutes later.

And it could have been a lot worse had Joe Willock not been caught fractionally offside by VAR after firing home in between those strikes.





Boos rang out around the stadium as Palace slumped to their fifth loss in eight games.

And the beautiful blue skies that looked down on Selhurst Park yesterday are now looking very stormy for Sage, who is only four months into a three-year contract.

Fans were already fuming after the 5-0 drubbing at bitter rivals Brighton last weekend.

But for Newcastle this was a huge win.



They had gone into this game on the back of three defeats in four games — and for the first half they were shocking.

The Geordies failed to register a single shot on target before a complete transformation after the break overpowered their hosts.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Jean-Philippe Mateta returned for Palace as one of three changes from the Brighton debacle.

Chris Richards was making his 100th Premier League appearance in this match.

Dan Burn was back to skipper Newcastle and making his first Prem start of the season after his late cameo up front from the bench against Aston Villa.



He was one of five changes with Fabian Schar, Jacob Murphy, Amar Dedic and William Osula all coming in.

Palace almost got off to a dream start when Adam Wharton’s free kick caused chaos in the Newcastle box.

The ball bounced all over the place before Mateta saw his powerful shot kept out by Lukas Hornicek.

Alarm bells must have been ringing for Matthias Jaissle with the manner in which Newcastle were being cut to pieces on the break.

After Toon lost possession on the halfway line, Mateta’s nice touch set Dwight McNeil away. He slipped through Daichi Kamada but the Japanese star dragged his shot wide.



The only positive for Newcastle was William Osula’s willingness to get into good positions out wide — and he almost benefitted when he dispossessed Wharton but his shot was blocked by Axel Disasi.

Yeremy Pino found a gap between Schar and Burn for Mateta to exploit.

And the French striker latched on to his fantastic pass but his shot whistled wide from the edge of the box.



Then McNeil raced down the left side of the Newcastle box and he fired the ball across the face of goal.

Newcastle’s wastefulness in attacking areas was brought into sharp focus when they won a free-kick in a dangerous position to the right of the Palace box.

Jacob Murphy worked the ball back to Barnes 30 yards from goal — but after he took an initial touch McNeil was there to dispossess him and start another break.

Burn must have wondered why he had bothered venturing up for a free-kick which surely should have been aimed at him.

However the big centre-half should have done better moments later.



Schar played a free-kick out wide for Lewis Hall and his cross was met by Burn but he could not get enough power or direction to trouble Walter Benitez.

Palace were not far away from moving in front when Pino whipped in a superb cross. Burn left it but fortunately for him it bounced into Hornicek’s grateful gloves.

Then Pino was fuming when he tried to latch on to a cut back from Kamada on the edge of the box but ref Paul Tierney got in his way.

After the break Newcastle swept in front.

This time Murphy produced a superb cross from the right and Osula was there to prod home.



And in a blink of an eye it looked like the Toon had doubled their lead.

Joelinton’s through ball was a peach for Willock to run on to and fire past Benitez.

But the Newcastle man had strayed inches offside.



The visitors were on top at this point and duly added their second.

Nico Gonzalez did well to keep the ball before finding Murphy.

He slipped in Amar Dedic, who squared a pass for Barnes to belt a shot past Benitez from 12 yards.

Boos rang out around Selhurst Park as the Toon Army celebrated.

Wharton tried to get Palace going again but his effort down the other end was palmed around the post by Hornicek.



But it was Newcastle who kept pressing and Joelinton blazed over from just inside the box.

Hornicek then managed to push wide a 25-yard belter from sub Dario Osorio.

The Palace attacker then blazed over from the edge of the box.

Sports.title: Hull 1 Brentford 1: Defensive horror show hands Bees battling point after McBurnie’s early penalty

OLI McBURNIE bagged his first Premier League goal in two years – but it wasn’t enough to halt Hull’s winless run as Brentford battled back for a point.

The 30-year-old struck 19 times last season and was the play-off final match winner to haul the Tigers back into the top flight against all odds.



But the striker had gone a worrying eight Prem games without a goal, and his last one came in a 2-2 draw for old club Sheffield United against Chelsea in April 2024.

McBurnie, whose renaissance has also led to a Scotland recall, banished the doubts with the 24th-minute opener.





But Dango Ouattara’s 63rd-minute equaliser – his first of the season – made it six league games without a victory for Sergej Jakirovic’s men.

Keith Andrews’ side showed more quality after the break but remain without an away win since beating Burnley back in February.

He will not have been happy by the barmy defending from the Bees that led to Hull’s breakthrough.

From a goal-kick played sideways to him, keeper Caoimhin Kelleher played a short pass out to Aaron Hickey.



In nipped an alert Tim Iroegbunam to pounce and was caught from behind by the Scotland international.

Referee Robert Jones pointed to the spot, booked Hickey, and McBurnie remained calm after a VAR check to confidently slot past Kelleher.

It was his fourth successful penalty for the Tigers since he joined them in 2025 and showed his relish for putting himself in the spotlight despite his barren run.

Until then, there had been little to excite a crowd who had braved the wild weather and turnstile issues to witness the first top-flight meeting between the teams.



Mohamed Belloumi whipped a free-kick over at one end, while Hickey fired straight at Hull keeper Konstantis Tzolakis after being teed up by Ouattara.

Hull were hammered 5-1 here the last time these sides met six years ago in the Championship.

But they are made of sterner stuff these days, especially at home, and showed the defensive defiance that helped them pick up five points in their three games against Manchester United, Aston Villa and Everton.

Semi Ajayi was typically robust and made a timely interception to cut out a cross as Igor Thiago looked poised to finish.

The big Brazilian striker then got in the way of a Kevin Schade strike just before the break after more good work down the right by Ouattara.



After 22 league goals in the last campaign, Thiago has failed to replicate the form that made him one of the division’s leading marksmen and booked him a place at the World Cup for his country.

But he did make a crucial contribution to his side’s cause, providing the assist to Ouattara for a tap-in after a deep cross had been flicked on to cause panic in the Hull box.

That sparked a welcome flurry of opportunities, with substitute Jaidon Anthony lashing wide and then having a header saved by Tzolakis.

Hull sub Mohamed-Ali Cho also had an effort saved by Kelleher, while Belloumi’s bag of tricks led to another dangerous break but a wild shot over the bar.

But the Seagulls were blown away thanks to two disastrous defensive blunders that followed a shocking miss at the other end.

For Yasin Ayari could so easily have changed the face of this fixture as Brighton, with 34 goals scored, cut their opponents only 14 minutes in.

Diego Gomez played the ball behind Virgil van Dijk, Gross crossed from the right flank and all Ayari really had to do was get his strike on target with Allison stranded.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But the Swede leaned back and lifted his effort two yards over the bar. Little did Hurzeler know it, but that was only the start of a horror spell that would destroy his side.

For it was the first of three self–inflicted wounds for there didn’t seem to be that much danger as Ronald Araujo crossed low as Liverpool tried to gain a first foothold.

Gross only needed to find Row Z at worst but he fired straight at Wirtz who instantly got over the shock of being presented with such a gift.

His shot wasn’t great but the ball cannoned off his fellow-countryman.

Bart Verbruggen had no chance of preventing the first goal Brighton conceded in over NINE hours over the magical charge that had been blitzing just about everyone in their sights.



It only got worse thanks to yet another catastrophic mistake even if Isak did punish it in some style.

Barcola charged down another attempted clearance, this time from Olivier Boscagli and again on Brighton’s left flank.

The Frenchman made the most of the mistake, delivering the kind of cross that helped him to back–to–back Champions League triumphs with Paris Saint-Germain.



Isak, now looking like the goal machine that prompted that British record £130M move from Newcastle at the start of last season, finished in stunning style.

Between those goals, Cody Gakpo demanded a fine parry from Verbruggen.

The Seagulls were all at sea. They had won four Prem games on the bounce in the shape of 5–0 against Coventry City, 3–0 against Arsenal, 2–0 at Sunderland and 5–0 in the trouncing of Crystal Palace.



But maybe they had begun to think that it was just too easy. As reality checks go, this was a crushing reminder that basics are required just as much as brilliance.

They would have been three down by the break but for another excellent stop, this time from Araujo’s drive, as Verbruggen at least performed with distinction.

Brighton’s best–ever start to a top-flight campaign with 23 goals scored was not exactly ruined as a result of excellence from their opponents.

True enough, Isak did take his opportunity with aplomb to claim his sixth Prem goal in six games, and Gakpo and Araujo produced explosive moments.

But the early chance spurned by Ayari only reinforced Kop fears that their heroes remain too easy to be picked off and four goals had been conceded in the four previous games.



Brighton will have gone into the game well–versed on Liverpool’s defensive deficiencies and to their credit they didn’t drop their heads – or lose belief that they might yet rescue the situation.

Indeed, they should have halved the deficit midway through the second half thanks to the kind of scintillating passing movement that should have undone Liverpool early in the game.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But Max De Cuyper lost his cool at the crucial moment to blast wide.



A bit like some of his team-mates did during that nightmare first half.

Sports.title: Neville fears Carrick set to be sacked as Carra calls for decision tonight
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick looks poised to lose his job as Manchester United head coach following their 3-0 defeat at Old Trafford to Bournemouth, according to Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher.

The humbling defeat leaves United just above the relegation zone following their worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

"It is going to get ridiculously difficult for Michael Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. That's the problem the club have got," said Neville during Sky Sports' match commentary.

On his podcast, Neville concluded: "They are probably going to sack him."

Carrick struck a defiant tone after the game but his lengthy applause towards the United fans after the final whistle was immediately interpreted as a farewell gesture.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carrick was applauded off the Old Trafford pitch following defeat to Bournemouth, but the same couldn't be said about the Manchester United players

"Michael Carrick needs to be relieved of his duties tonight," added Jamie Carragher. "Not just for the good of Manchester United but also for the good of Michael Carrick.

"Manchester United need to make that decision tonight."

Carrick led United to Champions League football after taking over from Ruben Amorim in mid-season last year, but United are winless in their last eight matches amid a wretched start to the current campaign.

"I did think last season that the club should have gone for the best manager they could have got and not given the job to Michael Carrick because I felt this might happen. But this has gone very, very sour very quickly and the club is a mess," said Neville.

Carrick's name was chanted loudly by the Old Trafford faithful following Bournemouth's game-sealing third goal but Neville fears that time may already be up for his former team-mate.

"Carrick is popular. But the owners, the sporting department and the players are not popular. They have badly let the club down.

"Tomorrow, they will probably make a decision that will disgust Manchester United fans but it is probably necessary.

"The Manchester United fans are singing Carrick's name because the reality tomorrow is: will he be the manager?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick explains why he dropped captain Bruno Fernandes

Bruno Fernandes was dropped from the match on Sunday after he criticised Carrick's tactics in the wake of Wednesday's 4-1 thrashing at Como in the Champions League. Surprisingly, the United captain stayed on the bench for the entirety of the defeat to Bournemouth.

It's become untenable," summarised Carragher. "Carrick wants to be changed. He doesn't want to be sat in the dugout with those players.

"Can you imagine going into the training ground tomorrow with Bruno Fernandes after not bringing him on? It's a rancid dressing room. He wants to be put out of his misery tonight."

Sports.title: Isak on target again as Liverpool beat Brighton
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak scored for a third straight Premier League game as Liverpool inflicted only Brighton's second loss of the season.

Isak's goal, finished emphatically from Bradley Barcola's right-wing cut-back, came four first-half minutes after Pascal Gross had diverted a Florian Wirtz shot into his own net.

Brighton arrived at Anfield having scored 23 goals in their first seven games of the season but lacked a clinical edge, with Yasin Ayari blazing a golden chance over moments before the opener.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pascal Gross deflected in Florian Wirtz's shot for the opener

Ayari later struck the post with a curling effort from outside the box as Brighton finished the game with only one shot on target despite having 64 per cent of the possession.

Trey Nyoni, a second-half substitute for Wirtz, who went down the tunnel after taking a knock to his ankle, also made a crucial, last-ditch tackle to deny Maxim De Cuyper in the Liverpool box.

The hosts had chances to add to their lead, wasting several counter-attacks and drawing Bart Verbruggen saves from Ronald Araujo and Cody Gakpo. But their first-half flurry proved sufficient to secure a first Premier League home win under Andoni Iraola.

The result takes them above Chelsea into fourth in the Premier League, only a point behind Brighton, who taste defeat for the first time since August. Liverpool's fourth win in a row in all competitions also provides further evidence of their attack finally clicking.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexander Isak buried Bradley Barcola's cut-back for the second goal

Isak's goal, his sixth of the season in the Premier League, came after fine work by summer signing Barcola, who stole possession high up the pitch before driving forward and picking out his team-mate.

Iraola starting to put his stamp on Liverpool

Momentum is building for Liverpool under Iraola. It's four wins in a row now and eight in 10 going back to the start of September.

They had to ride their luck at times. Brighton should have been in front before their opener. But the hosts were rewarded for attacking quickly and directly, in the style of their head coach.

Liverpool won possession in the final third five times - their second-highest total in the Premier League this season. Iraola values speed and incisiveness above possession, so the fact they had a meagre share of the ball is unlikely to concern him.

Image: Ferdi Kadioglu and Ryan Gravenberch battle for possession early on at Anfield

Instead, he will take satisfaction from the contributions of his attacking players. Barcola provided an assist for a second straight Premier League game, this time having been swapped to the right flank. Isak led the line with another clinical display.

Wirtz had bright moments too, taking the shot that forced the opening goal before coming off in the second half, while Rio Ngumoha, their star man in the midweek win over Villarreal, was only needed for a quarter of an hour with Gakpo also impressing.

Wirtz downplays injury fears Florian Wirtz insisted the injury that forced him off against Brighton is not serious.



The Liverpool playmaker had be be replaced by Trey Nyoni after appearing to hurt his ankle.



"I think it will be alright, it's not too bad," he said. "I don't know much yet. We still have to check it but I think it's not going to take long."

Iraola: We are playing with collective spirit

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola speaking to Sky Sports:

"Very happy. We needed this win at home and to celebrate with the supporters. A really good performance.

"We started really aggressively and needed this start because we had been coming from behind lately. Especially against a team full of confidence like Brighton, we were very focused on starting well, scoring first and, luckily for us, we did it.

"This is the fourth win in a row, it feels good. We have to keep going, we still have points to recover but I'm liking a lot of things.

"Good performances from the players, they are helping each other, we are playing together with collectiveness. Some of the players will have better or worse performances, but today it was a team that you can trust."

On Wirtz's injury: "He had to leave the pitch with a small twist of the ankle. It doesn't look very big but we're playing every three days so we have to see what it is.

"I don't know if it is even an injury. He twisted his ankle and it's painful in the moment and he didn't feel 100 per cent. We decided to put on Trey and he played a good performance."

Hurzeler: Only one team was playing to win

Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler speaking to Sky Sports:

"It was a missed opportunity.

"Everyone felt we could definitely take something away from this game. We came here to play our way. We made two easy mistakes to give them a present to score two goals.

"We had plenty of chances to score. We kept trying. They defended well in the box and have individual quality. We did everything. We have to avoid easy mistakes. We had chances but didn't have luck on our side today.

"We had a big chance with Yasin. If that goes in, the game is completely different. We have to learn we don't have to chase the game.

"We lost our structure a little bit at 2-0 down. We wanted to come back as quickly as possible and lost our structure. That's what we have to analyse and do better.

"In the second half, and also a lot of phases in the first-half, only one team was playing and trying to win."

Liverpool's low possession - Opta stats

Liverpool's possession of 35.6 per cent was their second lowest on record (since 2003/04) in a Premier League home win, and their lowest in an Anfield league victory since November 2010.

Only Erling Haaland (nine) has scored more Premier League goals this season than Liverpool's Alexander Isak (six), who has scored in three consecutive appearances in the competition for the first time since January 2025.

Liverpool have now benefitted from 80 own goals in the Premier League, the joint-most alongside Manchester United.

Sports.title: Drumbeat adds to O'Brien's two-year-old roll of honour
Sports.content:
Drumbeat added further depth to Aidan O'Brien's Classic battalion for next year in earning quotes of 14-1 for the Derby after landing the Criterium de Saint-Cloud at the Paris track.

The Wootton Bassett colt - wide-margin winner of the Zetland Stakes at Newmarket last time out - looked short of room at a crucial stage of the race under Ryan Moore, but burst through a gap to lead approaching a furlong and a half out.

From there he stayed on too strongly for stablemate Shakespeare and Christophe Soumillon, the pair two lengths back in second with Joseph O'Brien's Jesus Green a further length away in third.

The 9-10 favourite was delivering a seventh win in the race for O'Brien, but a first for Moore after wins for Soumillon aboard Pierre Bonnard 12 months ago and Los Angeles in 2023.

"He showed a lot of quality and is a very straightforward horse," Moore told Sky Sports Racing.

"He had the pace to go and take the gap and he quickened up well."

Sports.title: Littler's Euro dreams ended by shock defeat to Ratajski
Sports.content:
Luke Littler suffered a shock defeat to Krzysztof Ratajski at the European Championship Darts, as he failed in his attempt to claim the one major title he's never won.

The world No 1 was beaten 10-6 in the quarter-finals on Sunday afternoon as his bid to sweep all of the PDC's major titles before his 20th birthday fell short.

Poland's Ratajski remarkably won seven legs in a row to take a 7-1 lead over the world champion before Littler rallied to pull the game back to 8-6.

But he missed bullseye to hold throw in the 15th leg and Ratajski pinned D16 to move 9-6 ahead.

Littler then failed to take out 121 in the next leg and Ratajski hit D10 to beat The Nuke for the first time in eight meetings.

Following his defeat, Littler posted on social media to say: "Played well in the lead up to today, but just didn't click for me earlier.

"Thank you for all the support this weekend. The wait for this one goes on."

Littler produced the second-best average in the tournament's history against Nathan Aspinall on Saturday evening, but averaged less than 100 on Sunday and hit only six of 16 attempts at double.

It's the latest setback for Littler, who suffered early exits at the World Series of Darts Finals and the World Grand Prix in recent weeks.

Littler will appear on a Netflix special next Friday night when 20 amateur players will attempt to beat him over one leg to win £501,000 before he turns his attention to defending his Grand Slam of Darts title live on Sky Sports in November.

Reflecting on his victory, Ratajski said: "He started to play very well after the second break. It was 8-2 for me and I had to wait, play my game and focus on my throw.

"He won three or four legs in a row and then I took a chance when he missed a double seven. It was my chance and I took it.

"It's my biggest achievement in the European Championship."

European Championship: Sunday afternoon's results

Quarter-finals

Ross Smith 10-6 Luke Woodhouse Gerwyn Price 10-3 Stephen Bunting Martin Schindler 10-1 Jonny Clayton Krzysztof Ratajski 10-6 Luke Littler

Ratajski to face German favourite in last four

Ratajski will face a home favourite in the semi-finals after Martin Schindler produced an astonishing display to thrash Jonny Clayton 10-1.

In front of a raucous home support, the underdog reeled off nine legs in a row, including a 127 on the bull in the fifth leg and a 167 on the bull in the sixth.

Schindler didn't miss a double in the first seven legs of the match and averaged more than 103 as he pulled off one of the biggest wins of his career.

On the other side of the draw, Gerwyn Price crushed Stephen Bunting 10-3 to book his place in Sunday evening's semi-finals.

Price went eight darts into a nine-darter in the fourth leg of the match, only to miss D12 for the perfect leg. However, he romped into a 7-1 lead and rarely looked in trouble.

Bunting briefly rallied to recover to 7-3, but Price reeled off three more legs for a comprehensive win with a 103 average.

Price will face top seed Ross Smith, who remains in the hunt for a second European Championship title after an impressive 10-6 victory over Luke Woodhouse in the opening match of the day.

He averaged 107 and hit seven 180s before sealing victory in style with a bullseye finish.

21m ago 13.21 EDT Half-time reading When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” The switch of venue to England from its usual home in Paris is a mark of respect to the man who became the first active player to receive a knighthood in 1965, a few months before retiring at the age of 50. It also provides an opportunity to recall an astonishing career that began with his local side Stoke in 1932 and made the “Wizard of Dribble” the most famous player on the planet. Sports.title: Michael Carrick on the brink after Manchester United are humiliated by Bournemouth
Sports.content:
After Bruno Fernandes was dropped for “pure football” reasons – according to Michael Carrick – could Manchester United actually win a game of football?

The answer, again, was a resounding, humiliating no, and if the manager’s job remains in real peril, you have to wonder, too, if this beleaguered team should steel themselves for a relegation dogfight. They lack imagination, cohesion, fight, confidence and anything resembling joy, and so, now they hover a point above the drop zone, survival cannot be taken for granted.

Goals from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson downed United this afternoon yet what has killed Carrick and side in the past fortnight is the insubordination of Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez plus the deeper malaise of a club that is riven by factions.

The Sir Jim Ratcliffe-led football department may issue Carrick the bullet but the next man – Eddie Howe is favoured and is open to the job – will surely not break the boom-bust cycle that is each new manager’s fate. Before this latest debacle, you had to flick the calendar back 45 days to 10 September (eight games ago), for the last time United chalked up a “W” and gave their fans reason to cheer.

Once more Carrick’s men failed to do so. Equally as disappointing is how, in the days since Fernandes’s public takedown of Carrick, no apology has been forthcoming from the captain.

Where Martínez did say sorry for criticising Jason Wilcox (though, not to the director of football), the United captain’s silence speaks volumes. If Carrick made an error in not dropping Martínez for his outburst, discarding Fernandes was the correct call and so Harry Maguire’s redemption arc was complete, being handed the armband, after it was taken off him and given to the Portuguese in July 2023.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes stayed on the bench throughout having been dropped. Harry Maguire captained the side instead. Photograph: Gary Oakley/EPA

Now, Carrick surely fears being removed after a buoyant Bournemouth made it four successive wins versus an opponent offering scant resistance, as the boos ringing out at the end signified.

As is the case for this Carrick iteration, midfield control was an issue throughout. Youri Tielemans lost the ball, Bournemouth’s passing went tap-tap-tap, and United were turned.

Even when Leny Yoro fashioned a one-two with Tielemans and swept the ball left to Diogo Dalot, the move foundered, and moments later the young right-back was clearing from beneath his bar as a Rayan cross went close to teeing Evanilson up. All of this, yet again, pointed to a team that seem unable to execute whatever Carrick’s plan is.

Senne Lammens would hoof upfield aimlessly, Maguire would head possession back to a white shirt instead of chesting down, and as the half hour passed a wild Dalot shot was their sole one registered.

When Bournemouth scored it was due to United shooting themselves in both feet. First came Ayden Heaven’s wild scissor challenge that had Evanilson leaping out of danger and was adjudged a yellow-card offence.

View image in fullscreen Bournemouth’s Evanilson watches his brilliant finish hit the net to make it 3-0 at Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters

The second self-inflicted moment came when Justin Kluivert’s free-kick, on a diagonal from Bournemouth’s right, was allowed to drop on Rayan’s boot freely with the Brazilian entirely unmarked.

“Sacked in the mornin cog” came the derisory chants from the travelling faithful and when their men doubled their lead on 42 minutes you wondered if Carrick might not last until then.

Again, this should have been avoided. This time Yoro was to blame as he contrived to slip near United’s area, allowing Adrien Truffert to collect; the left-back squared to Tavernier, who slid into the net.

Cue the unfurling of a Stretford End tifo that said: “STANDARDS” above the faces of Eric Cantona, Bryan Robson and Roy Keane, the Cherries congregation this time offering, “going down with the City”, on repeat.

Carrick’s move for a second half that might decide his fate was to take off Tielemans for Matheus Cunha, Mason Mount (anonymous again), taking the No 10 position. If the manager had, indeed, dropped Fernandes for his form, then the opening period was a fair argument to reinstate him. Yet if Rayan had not fluffed a simple chance to make it 3-0 – the attempt was a pea-roller – even the mutineer would not be able to save United.

Next, though, it was game – and possibly Carrick’s tenure – over. Lammens charged out to clear a through ball, Evanilson beat him to it, rounded the flailing No 1, and from around 40 yards out on the right sliced a curving finish into the waiting net.

Carrick’s visage was a picture of hurt. On the bench, Fernandes zipped his top right up, while in his posh seat, Wilcox sank lower into his winter coat. This would not stop him hearing, towards the end, abusive chants directed towards him. They were cruel, but there is true pain being felt in these parts.

Sports.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
Sports.content:
Brighton’s emphatic run was blown off course at Anfield as Liverpool moved up to fourth with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It is Liverpool, convincing winners on home soil for the first time this season in the Premier League, who looked upwardly mobile.

Florian Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Alexander Isak converted his sixth league goal of the campaign to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive Premier League wins. Brighton’s winning streak had included 15 goals and none against but there was neither attacking verve nor defensive resilience on show from Fabian Hürzeler’s side. Liverpool had a monopoly on both, and the sight of Bradley Barcola racing back to defend and Ronald Araújo thundering into challenges will have satisified Iraola just as much as the incisiveness up front.

Storm Boelo raged outside the stadium but inside it was relatively calm, vindicating the decision to proceed with the game. But not for Brighton. The run of wins and clean sheets that had swept Hurzeler’s team into third place before kick off was devastated by Liverpool’s attacking force. The home side’s superior first half performance was another demonstration of the expensive trio of Wirtz, Isak and Barcola feeling increasingly at home under Iraola.

Liverpool were aggressive and sharp from the start, in contrast to their opening against Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday, and opened the scoring just as Brighton were beginning to exert their first serious spell of pressure.

There was an element of good fortune about the breakthrough but it also encapsulated the differing intensity between the teams when Wirtz held off Lewis Dunk and Araújo beat both the Brighton captain and Oliver Boscagli to the loose ball. His low cross pin-balled off two Brighton players before rebounding to Wirtz, whose first time shot deceived Bart Verbruggen via another deflection off Gross. Wirtz’s low key celebration hinted at what was to come. It was not his first league goal of the campaign and second goal in successive games after all. The breakthrough was officially credited as an own goal from the Brighton midfielder.

It should also have been a Liverpool equaliser rather than the opener as Yasin Ayari had a glorious chance to give Brighton the lead moments earlier. Diego Gómez and Gross combined to pierce Liverpool’s left flank and present Ayari with a free sight of goal with Alisson dragged across to his left. The Brighton forward blazed high into the Kop and would soon have added reason to rue the miscue.

Liverpool quickly doubled their lead when capitalising on more casual Brighton defending. Boscagli was again found wanting when attempting to deal with Alisson’s clearance deep into the visitors’ half. The left-back struck a clearance straight at Barcola and was then left floundering as the France international, deployed on the right, brushed aside his efforts to recover possession. Isak steered Barcola’s delivery inside the far corner with a deft, side-foot finish to score in three consecutive league games for the first time since January 2025. It was Liverpool’s first goal scored by a Liverpool player in the first half of a Premier League game at Anfield this season. There was no surprise whatsoever when Boscagli was withdrawn at half-time.

Brighton attacked with greater conviction than they defended but with Araújo, Jérémy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk all making telling interventions, and receiving impressive support from all quarters, Alisson was not seriously tested. The visitors’ best hope of a recovery stemmed from the Liverpool keeper’s own risky pass to Alexis Mac Allister, which gifted possession back to Brighton and resulted in Ayari striking a post from 20 yards out.
