Jack Hinshelwood, Boscagli’s replacement, and fellow substitute Malick Yalcouyé injected more energy and bite into Brighton’s second half display but an end product from the visitors remained lacking. Too many overhit crosses and poor final balls enabled Liverpool to protect their lead in comfort.

Sports.title: Osula and Barnes’ second-half burst sees Newcastle pile pressure on lacklustre Palace
Sports.content:
The first half was one of the worst 45 minutes of football in Premier League history. The pass completion rate was a meagre 72.8%, although it felt lower. There were only two shots on target. The sun kept popping out from behind the clouds to take a look, and then going back in again, appalled. And the really bad news for Crystal Palace is that, for them, that was the good bit.

Newcastle were much improved after the break. Will Osula touched in a Jacob Murphy cross two minutes after half-time, Joe Willock had an effort ruled out for a marginal offside five minutes later, and Harvey Barnes completed a slick passing move six minutes after that. A smattering of boos from the home fans made clear what everybody already knew. Quarter of an hour of proper football had been enough to win the game, and that leaves Pierre Sage under significant pressure.

To an extent he is a victim of circumstance. Palace are listing after summer sales, Maxence Lacroix and Daniel Muñoz joining the familiar exodus. Two wins in eight league games is troubling, particularly when one of them was as freakish as the previous home game against Nottingham Forest, when they were outplayed for much of the first half and inexplicably went in ahead at half-time. Nobody could have drawn much confidence from that, and the shellacking they sustained at Brighton last week is the kind of thing that might have got a manager more than a few weeks in the job the sack.

There were a couple of early chances. Daichi Kamada sliced his finish after a promising run by Dwight McNeil. Jean-Philippe Mateta, so devastating when Palace beat Newcastle in April, dragged a shot wide. McNeil rolled a low pass through a vacant six-yard box after good work from Yéremy Pino. But that golden age of incident soon passed.

View image in fullscreen Pierre Sage has struggled since taking over as Crystal Palace manager from Oliver Glasner. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

By the quarter hour an eerie silence had already fallen over Selhurst Park. It was not just that nothing was happening, it was that there was no expectation of anything happening. In part it was the blustery wind on a chilly autumnal afternoon, but there was also the sense that these are two fundamentally ordinary sides, low on confidence, coming to terms with new managers, neither of whom can have a huge amount of confidence they will still be in their roles in a couple of months. No weather conditions can explain why so many basic passes were misplaced, why the ball spent so much time bouncing aimlessly around the centre-circle, or why shots kept being struck into players a couple of feet away.

And that is the other worry for Palace. This wasn’t a defeat to a high-flyer or a team in form. After a mildly promising start to the season, anxiety had begun to set in for Newcastle. They were booed off after last week’s defeat at home to Aston Villa, their third defeat in four. Losing to an improving Villa in itself is no disgrace; the issue was more the manner of it. Had it worked, the deployment of Dan Burn as an emergency centre-forward would have been hailed as inspired thinking; but it did not work – and, really, how likely was it to? – and so it looked like desperation.

The appeals for patience are reasonable enough: Mattias Jaissle has been in charge for only three months and replacing a manager who had been in charge for five years is rarely a straightforward process, even if the squad has not lost its three best players. But at the same time £260m was spent on eight signings, of whom only Nico González has made much of an impact so far, although Amar Dedic was solid enough here.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Burn, restored to the back four alongside Fabian Schär ahead of Sven Botman and Malick Thiaw, was immense, untroubled by the physicality of Mateta, of whom it may charitably be said that he is not back to his best after injury. The defence generally looked assured, while González was pretty much the only player in that chaotic first half who had any sense that some semblance of shape may be desirable. This is a squad that is still taking shape, with the new signings presumably to be introduced gradually but, ultimately, Newcastle should be comfortably mid-table.

It’s hard to have such confidence in Palace. Lukas Hornicek did have to make two saves around the mid-point of the second half, first from an Adam Wharton curler and then a long-range drive from Darío Osorio, but there was very little threat, very little imagination and very little quality from them. Newcastle were far from brilliant, but that 15-minute spell after half-time was more than enough to win the game comfortably. There is discontent at Palace, and it is justified.

Sports.title: Ouattara rescues point for Brentford as Hull maintain unbeaten home record
Sports.content:
Hull’s unbeaten home record remains intact but the Tigers have not tasted victory for seven games after a 1-1 draw with Brentford at the MKM Stadium.

The opening goal came courtesy of a 24th-minute Oli McBurnie penalty, awarded when Aaron Hickey flattened Tim Iroegbunam inside the area while trying to hook the ball away.

McBurnie picked out the bottom right of the net and though Brentford’s Caoimhin Kelleher guessed right, he could not stop McBurnie scoring his first Premier League goal for more than 900 days.

After the break, Hull were left to rue some inattentive defending as Igor Thiago found his way to Dango Ouattara, who slotted the ball home under very little pressure to make it 1-1 in the 63rd minute.

Jaidon Anthony pushed for a second Brentford goal and saw a shot land just wide before getting a second chance, which forced a save from Konstantinos Tzolakis, but there was a quick counter as Mohamed Belloumi raced in the other direction before firing over from distance.

An 88th-minute chance was Hull’s last to find the winning goal, but Mohamed-Ali Cho’s cross to Joe Gelhardt resulted in an off-target shot that ensured the Tigers took no more than a point as their wait for an away win continues.

Both clubs were required to pick through the detritus of the pre-match display in the opening minutes as balloons and litter were carried by the strong winds of Storm Boelo on to the pitch.

The first chance of note fell to the visitors, with Hull faltering in midfield after 11 minutes and allowing Hickey to unleash a shot that was comfortably dealt with by Tzolakis.

Ten minutes later, Belloumi found McBurnie inside the box, but as the Scot was preparing to strike, Brentford’s Mathias Jensen rushed forward to foil the attempt.

View image in fullscreen Oli McBurnie (left) hugs Mohamed Belloumi after putting Hull ahead from the penalty spot. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

After 22 minutes the visitors offered their hosts a golden chance when Hickey, having failed to collect a ball from Kelleher, lunged at the legs of Iroegbunam and floored him to give away a penalty. McBurnie stepped up and made no mistake, finding the bottom right of the net and putting the ball beyond Kelleher, despite the Brentford goalkeeper leaping in the correct direction.

After the break Brentford broke through. In the 63rd minute, Ouattara made the most of lax Hull defending to collect an Igor Thiago ball and tap home.

Belloumi then reacted with a sprint towards the Brentford goal with substitute Cho in pursuit as back up, but the long-range shot was too high and flew into the stand.

The final roll of the dice was Cho’s cross in to Gelhardt, but he was wide of the mark and the whistle blew on a 1-1 draw that maintains unbeaten records home and away.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibernian
Sports.content:
Camilo Durán moved into double figures for the season as Celtic reasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleaguered Hibernian 2-1 at windy Easter Road.

After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break.

It proved enough to secure a ninth win in 10 league games and ensure the recently appointed home boss, Marink Reedijk, suffered a third straight defeat since succeeding David Gray.

There were a couple of blemishes for Celtic, however, as substitute Alistair Johnston’s return from injury lasted barely 20 minutes before he had to go off, while £11million forward Kasper Hogh – restored to the starting line-up after notching in just one of his 13 previous matches for the Hoops – again drew a blank before being replaced in the 64th minute.

Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 win at Ibrox on Saturday. After dropping two points at Dundee, the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from the Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy.

Saints started the second half brightly but goals from the Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. The Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on the midfielder Nico Raskin, before the substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining.

View image in fullscreen Rangers’ Kevin Kelsy scores the third goal against St Johnstone. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

McInnes said: “It’s quite ironic in the sense that we were so good and so brilliant at times in the first half and create so many opportunities, that we were only a goal to the good at half-time. And obviously, we don’t want to let the frustration of those missed opportunities and dominance filter into the second half.

“I think half-time came at a bad time for us because, despite the conditions, some of the play was really good. I asked the players to be brilliant today, not just win the game, can we really commit to being the best we can be, as good as we can be? And I thought we were in the first half. Everything was brilliant except the result at half-time because we should have been more in in front.”

Dundee United won a rollercoaster game 3-2 against Aberdeen at Tannadice. Zidane Iqbal scored for the hosts before the visitors equalised through Nesta Guinness-Walker – both players scoring their first goals for their clubs.

United took the lead once more thanks to a Dylan Tait strike, with Connor Ronan drawing Aberdeen level after the break. Zac Sapsford secured all three points for his side, with the win moving United up to fourth – one point behind Hearts, who are at Motherwell on Sunday – while Aberdeen dropped to ninth.

Two own goals helped Falkirk climb to seventh with a 3-0 victory over Kilmarnock. Centre-backs Cathal McCarthy and George Stanger scored past their own goalkeeper either side of a Jacob Murrell header. St Mirren ended their losing streak with a 2-1 victory over Dundee with goals from Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule before Bradley Fink pulled one back for the visitors.

Sports.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
Sports.content:
In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.”

To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest.

The clip was widely shared, there is every chance you saw it this month. The general perception, from those of a neutral stance, was that one of football’s great characters had lost the plot. To those in the room, there was a sense that it was merely the exuberant mannerisms of a quirky manager during a tricky period. But for a large section of Swindon fans, it prompted an unamused eye roll. Here we go again. The circus tent is pitched firmly in town.

Supporting a Holloway-led club is an interesting assignment. Within weeks of taking the Swindon job two years ago on Sunday, he began constructing a hostile wall towards fans by reminding them that they could “go bowling” if they did not like his methods. Last December, he had to be restrained by his players during an altercation with a fan, while he has made a habit of telling them to “jog on” if overly vocal in their criticism.

When his side picked up a much-needed point against Walsall last week, the goalkeeping coach held him back from another confrontation with supporters. Asked about it, he goaded reporters into putting his address online so that disgruntled fans could have it out with him: “I don’t really care anymore.” So, when season‑ticket holders found their phones pinging with amused messages containing the same viral Holloway zombie clip, their lack of laughter could be forgiven.

“When you get these soundbites from Ian Holloway, outside the Swindon Town world it’s all about what a great character he is, how he says it like it is, and how it must be great to have him as manager,” says Rich Pullen, founder and co-host of the largest Swindon podcast, Loathed Strangers. “But, to a growing percentage of the Swindon community, it’s exhausting and it takes away from any of the good.

“If Swindon win, post-match he often uses it as an opportunity to have a go at the fans. It’s got to the stage where you can’t even enjoy a win without Ian Holloway being unable to hold himself from criticising fans. The easy thing to do is ignore him, but it’s almost impossible because he is everywhere. He goes viral and everyone always thinks: ‘Oh, isn’t that funny.’ Well, no. People are tired of the excess noise.”

View image in fullscreen Disheartened Swindon fans stand solemnly in the pouring rain at the Memorial Stadium. Photograph: Jeremy Landey/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

This time last week, there was a thought that the M4 derby homecoming trip to Bristol Rovers on Saturday might hasten a possible end to Holloway’s Swindon tenure. Winless in eight games in all competitions, the discontent was not expected to abate on the preceding midweek trip to high-flying Barnet. The 3-1 victory that followed – Barnet’s first league defeat of the season – was a huge shock, thanks in no small part to the heroics of the goalkeeper, Connor Ripley, who recently declared the whole squad would “run through a brick wall” for Holloway.

Swindon might have followed it with another win, at Rovers’ Memorial Stadium, only for Matty Virtue to miss an open goal 90 seconds into the match. The forgettable goalless draw that played out at least extended Swindon’s unbeaten run to three games and kept them safely mid-table in League Two. Holloway was right to savour the improved performances, but the malaise runs deeper.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The manager had said something far more significant immediately after his viral soundbite when he continued: “The owner’s a dead man walking as well and that over‑complicates everything here.”

Even those seeking a more composed figure in Holloway’s place agree the manager is just one cog in a machine many argue has been misfiring for some time. Days after the zombie rant, the Swindon Town Supporters Trust declared the club had “lost our soul, our hope, our passion”, and urged Holloway’s comments about the Australian owner, Clem Morfuni, to “be a wake-up call”.

Since saving the club from probable administration in 2021, Morfuni has become a target of increasing fan indignation, failing to sell up and adding millions to the club’s debt. “Whilst the short-term focus may be on Ian Holloway, the bigger picture is above the role of the manager,” concluded the Trust, pointing to “a wedge with supporters so obvious that even the manager openly talks about it”.

In such a context, the uptick in form is merely one – albeit very welcome – aspect among wider misgivings. Because what fans really want is a united club and manager they can get behind; not to go jogging on.

Sports.title: Relief for Slegers as Russo rescues Arsenal against Tottenham in WSL
Sports.content:
Alessia Russo’s contentious second-half penalty delivered relief, a reprieve and a chance for a reset as Arsenal came from a goal down to earn their second win of the WSL season in the north London derby.

At a rain-lashed Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Gunners were again their own worst enemy, forced to come from behind after Cathinka Tandberg’s headed opener. Georgia Stanway levelled and Russo powered in the penalty that gave them the lead they protected defiantly.

The Tottenham manager, Martin Ho, queried the penalty decision, with the ball hitting the raised arm of substitute Ella Morris from the clearance of one of her teammates. “My interpretation of the rule is if your teammate hits it and it hits your player, if you’re one yard away, the time and distance is taken into account, so there’s no penalty,” he said. “That’s my understanding of it, from when we were told to start the season. I want to understand what they’re saying, because then I can accept the decision.

“I don’t want the game to be about that, but when it decides a game it’s frustrating because it’s not within the law of the game.”

Arsenal’s manager, Renée Slegers, said she was glad to give the fans a win. “They sing us and fight us through the game,” she said. “At the end it’s scrappy, it’s game management and it’s scenarios, and they’re all with us.”

With the pressure building on her and her players after five games without a win, at times it felt like they were trying to disprove the phrase “you can’t dig yourself out of a hole”.

Quick Guide Brighton cruise to victory against West Ham Show Maisie Symonds’ first-half stunner sent Brighton on their way to a 3-0 win against West Ham at the Amex Stadium. The midfielder Symonds’ thunderbolt gave the Seagulls a half-time lead before Fran Kirby and Kiko Seike struck quickfire goals midway through the second period. It was a first clean sheet this season for Arturo Ruiz’s side and lifts them up to eighth in the table, two points above West Ham, who slipped to 12th after their fifth league defeat of the campaign. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Arsenal had looked a little shaky in the opening few minutes but they settled, built possession and started to pose a threat. A failure to carve out clearcut chances and capitalise on any period of dominance has been the running theme of their season. They lacked fight and there was sloppiness too, with too many overhit passes putting the ball out of play or giving away possession.

That the opener came from a Tottenham corner was unsurprising. Victoria Pelova swung the ball in and Tandberg rose above her two markers, Stanway and Emily Fox, who failed to even to jump and challenge, and headed home.

Spurs’ joy was short lived as Stanway made up for her marking error four minutes later by arriving to meet Russo’s cut back and powered the ball in off the crossbar.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Georgia Stanway equalises for Arsenal in the 17th minute. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

After the break there was concern for Tottenham when Alice Sombath’s leg seemed to twist awkwardly as she stretched for the ball. The club’s record signing left on a stretcher to be replaced by Morris, who made her return from an anterior cruciate ligament injury towards the end of last season.

After the lengthy stoppage, Russo forced a huge save from Lize Kop as she attempted to turn in Caitlin Foord’s cross from close range, the forward putting her hands to her head and screaming in frustration at the missed opportunity.

It did not take long for that frustration to transform into elation. The resulting corner from Kyra Cooney-Cross was headed on by Leah Williamson at the near post and Lisa Baum’s effort came back off the post. Spurs’ clearance bounced off the raised arm of Morris and the referee pointed to the spot. Russo sent Kop the wrong way and drove the ball low into the corner.

Arsenal were clinging on as the final whistle loomed but they had “found their fight,” said Slegers. “We had a run of games where results haven’t been good enough. It was frustrating for everyone. I’m so happy we got to win on this occasion, in the north London derby, away from home in the rain and we showed that character in the team.

“This will definitely energise us. We need to back this up in the next couple of games.”

Sports.title: Every diabolical Man United player was a 0/10 and they revel in finding new ways to disgrace the badge
Sports.content:
Every diabolical Man United player was a 0/10 and they revel in finding new ways to disgrace the badge

A banner with Bryan Robson, Roy Keane and Eric Cantona on it unfurled after Bournemouth scored their abomination of a second goal said it all.

‘Standards’ it screamed in big red letters on a black background. The problem for Michael Carrick is that standards at Old Trafford have slipped so dramatically that nobody is remotely surprised to see Bournemouth come away with the points in a 3-0 victory.



5 Another week, another defeat for United as they extended their winless run to eight in all competitions Credit: AFP

In fact, the Cherries have now avoided defeat in their last seven meetings with United.

Like many of the so-called 'lesser teams' in the Premier League, the ground that Sir Alex Ferguson made a fortress has become the Cherries' playground.

Carrick looks certain now to pay the price for United's terrible run of form with his job and must be at a loss to explain how his team have regressed so quickly from the performances in the second half of last season that got him the gig in the first place.



Carrick made the bold call to drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench as punishment for his astonishing attack on his head coach in the wake of the mid-week drubbing at Como.

5 The United fans made a point of booing the players after Carrick went down the tunnel ahead of them Credit: AFP



Fernandes was joined among the subs by fellow bad boy Lisandro Martinez and Matheus Cunha, whose body language in recent weeks has done Carrick no favours.

But if Carrick was hoping his emotional pre-match press conference address would have a stirring impact on his players, he was sadly mistaken.



In the five-minute monologue, Carrick spoke about values and humility and claimed there was a ‘a resilience in this football club.’

Sadly, for the 2008 Champions League winner, his monstrosity of a team showed none of those qualities and produced a performance that would get most managers fired.

The simple fact is that these United players do not appear to hurt anywhere near as much as Carrick when they lose games or concede cheap goals.

If I didn’t know better, I would say they revel in finding new ways to humiliate themselves and to disgrace the badge that was once the pride of English football.



5 Carrick looks to be on his way out as United head coach, and none of his players did anything to help him Credit: Getty

How else do you explain the diabolical defending that allowed Rayan to ghost in at the far post and guide Justin Kluivert's free-kick into the bottom corner?

The immediate reaction laid bare the problem whoever replaces Carrick will have to solve.

There were no angry recriminations, no words exchanged, just a simple collective shrug of the shoulders. Even stand-in captain Harry Maguire had a look of resignation in his eyes.



If that wasn’t bad enough, there are almost no words to describe the lapse in concentration that saw Leny Yoro caught in possession and sent tumbling by Adrian Truffert in the lead up to Marcus Tavernier's tap-in second goal.

Yoro was regarded as one of the best up-and-coming players in Europe when United prised him away from French club Lille a couple of summers ago.

However, the 20-year-old has been dragged down to the same pitiful levels of most of his teammates.

5 Club captain Fernandes didn't even make it off the bench as United hit a new low just two months into the season Credit: AFP



Yoro is still on the radar of French giants Paris Saint-Germain and would be advised to ask his agent to get him as far away from United as quickly as possible.

Carrick is understood to have been enthused by the midfield rebuild United underwent in the summer, and particularly the arrival of £70million Carlos Baleba.

Baleba still looks some way short of full match sharpness but is far from the biggest problem when it comes to the middle of the park.

Carrick's faith in Baleba’s fellow summer signing Youri Tielemans has been misguided, and the Belgian was hooked at half-time after another shockingly abject performance.



How Chelsea persuaded United technical director Jason Wilcox to part with £50m for Andrey Santos is one of life’s mysteries. If United were operating as a serious football club they would not have gone near a cast-off from Stamford Bridge.

Carrick has undoubtedly been set up to fail by Wilcox and co. Not having a fit striker nor left-back for a game he simply to had to win is evidence of that.

5

Evanilson’s third goal after more criminal defending from a combination of Martinez and Harry Maguire was the final nail in Carrick’s coffin.



Whoever replaces him will be inheriting the most poisoned chalice in the Premier League. United are a club with no standards.

Sports.title: Manchester United relax controversial Old Trafford rule for one game only
Sports.content:
Manchester United relax controversial Old Trafford rule for one game only

Manchester United relaxed their rules on season ticket holders attending fixtures for the visit of Bournemouth on Sunday.

A change was confirmed prior to the match due to weather conditions in the North West amid Storm Boelo.



3 United relaxed rules on season ticket holders for the visit of Bournemouth Credit: Getty

The fixture took place during an amber weather warning for strong winds, with disruption to public transport and road closures expected.

As a result, longer journey times were anticipated in the area, causing some fans not to attend the match.

Red Devils relax rules

United subsequently will not count those absences against minimum usage figures for season ticket holders.



Failing to attend the match against the Cherries will also not affect fans' season ticket renewals.

The move was confirmed on social media by an independent supporter liaison officer.



Fans were also given the opportunity to transfer their ticket to the match to another official United member.

In a post on X, the independent supporter liaison officer said: "Following contact from supporters affected by travel disruption, we raised this with the club this morning and have received reassurance that missing today’s game because of weather-related cancellations will not count against minimum usage or affect season ticket renewal."



The forecasted windy conditions would remain beyond the start of the match at 2pm on Sunday afternoon.

First half goals from Rayan and Marcus Tavernier put the visitors in front as United fell 2-0 behind before the interval.

Evanilson later added a third for Bournemouth inside the final 20 minutes.

3 An amber weather warning caused disruption for those attending Old Trafford on Sunday Credit: Getty



The result sees United slip to 16th in the Premier League, just a point above the relegation zone.

Michael Carrick's side have now failed to win any of their last eight matches in all competitions.

United season ticket holders

United's move to relax rules on season ticket holders follows their controversial treatment of fans earlier this year.

The club were publicly criticised by multiple supporter groups in the summer.



It came after fans had their season ticket accounts restricted by the Red Devils.

Accounts were targeted where usernames and logins had been shared with more than six people.

3 Season ticket holders who missed the loss to Bournemouth will not have their accounts affected Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, United announced last month they had banned 685 season ticket holders.



The process was part of a club investigation into ticket touting.

Sports.title: Florian Wirtz has first Premier League goal of season taken off him before Liverpool injury
Sports.content:
Florian Wirtz has first Premier League goal of season taken off him before Liverpool injury

Florian Wirtz thought he opened his Premier League account for the season, but his wait goes on.

Liverpool went ahead against Brighton on Sunday after 17 minutes of play as Wirtz hit a first-time effort inside the area.

2 Wirtz appeared to have smashed in the opener for Liverpool, but his shot went off Gross for an own goal Credit: Getty

The Germany international has had a difficult second season with the Reds and already been linked with a move away from Anfield.

A goal will do him a world of good amid his £116.5million transfer fee.

However, he remains without a goal in the English top flight for the 2026/27 campaign.

Minutes after the opener, the Premier League revealed that the goal has been accredited to someone else.

"The goal accreditation panel has adjudged Liverpool's 17th minute goal as a Gross own goal."

Liverpool netted a second moments later as Alexander Isak found the target from a Bradley Barcola cross.

Wirtz appeared to pick up an injury shortly before the hour mark, but he was able to return to play.

However, he was substituted swiftly after and went straight down the tunnel.

Brighton had conceded just five goals and kept four clean sheets in the league before Sunday.

However, their defence was breached on two occasions in a matter of minutes and they no longer have the joint-best defence with Arsenal.

Sports.title: Man United ‘humiliate themselves’ as Michael Carrick told he’ll be sacked at full-time
Sports.content:
Man United ‘humiliate themselves’ as Michael Carrick told he’ll be sacked at full-time

Michael Carrick and his Manchester United team were booed off at half-time at Old Trafford.

The Red Devils were 2-0 down to Bournemouth in another embarrassing performance that they went on to lose 3-0.

2 Tavernier scored Bournemouth's second against Man United Credit: AFP

A comeback would have been a tall order seeing as the Cherries had never lost a Premier League game while two goals up at the break.

The under-pressure Carrick, who dropped captain Bruno Fernandes for the match, was told he was likely to be out of work come Monday morning.

talkSPORT's Micky Gray said: "Michael Carrick has 45 minutes to save his job."

But chief football correspondent Alex Crook surmised: “They find new ways to dishonour the badge, honestly from one to 11. They're not fit for purpose and Michael Carrick's got no chance. Micky says he's got 45 minutes to save his job. I think he's done."

Later in the second half, he said: "This could be a relegation battle for Man United. They are not just losing games, they are getting battered."

At the end of the game, Carrick completed a lap of Old Trafford before disappearing down the tunnel.

Once he had gone, the boos from the home fans towards the players were very loud.

Bournemouth at the triple

Ayden Heaven gave the ball away with a sloppy pass and then jumped in two-footed with a rash challenge to try and win it back.

He was saved by Evanilson pulling out of the duel, which means Heaven is only given a yellow, but his reprieve was short-lived.

The resulting free-kick was floated to the back post, and Rayan clinically finished past Senne Lammens inside his near post.

The worst was yet to come as Leny Yoro slipped while trying to play the ball on the edge of his own box.

Adrien Truffert ruthlessly punished him by taking over and squaring it for Tavernier to roll into an empty net.

In the second half, Evanilson made it 3-0 as he raced on to a long ball forward.

Senne Lammens came off his line, but he was too slow as the striker touched it past him and scored from a tight angle.

Fernandes dropped

Carrick made the bold call ahead of the match to drop Fernandes following his comments about Man United's tactics in midweek.

The Red Devils were crushed by Como 4-1 in the Champions League, and after the game, the captain questioned the idea not to press the Italian side.

Fernandes then trained as normal on Friday and Saturday before being left on the bench.

Speaking ahead of the match, Carrick revealed that he'd dropped the skipper for footballing reasons.

In his pre-match Sky Sports interview, he said: “Pure football.

"When you have options it's always a difficult decision.

“We have to make the right one for today and the team to get that performance we want."

2 Fernandes was left on the bench for the first time since 2021 against Villarreal Credit: Getty

Carrick even refused to rule out taking the captaincy off the Portuguese international.

He said: "The most important thing for me is the team, first and foremost, the squad and the dynamics in the squad.

"Again, it's about the football club, I'll always do what's best for the football club."

And he remained on the bench throughout.

Dreadful form

With Bournemouth's win, Man United are sitting in 16th place in the Premier League.

They are just one point above the drop zone and have won one game all season.

That was a 5-2 victory over Ipswich Town, and they haven't won since.

In all competitions, they only have one other victory that came against Sabah in the Champions League.

Sports.title: New footage shows Chelsea fans rowing with Levi Colwill moments after Tottenham loss
Sports.content:
New footage shows Chelsea fans rowing with Levi Colwill moments after Tottenham loss

Chelsea fans were spotted venting their frustrations with Levi Colwill following the shock 2-0 defeat to Tottenham.

Cole Palmer was sent off as the Blues suffered a third Premier League loss of the season at home against their bitter rivals.



2 Chelsea fans fumed as they watch their team lose at home to Spurs for the first time in eight years Credit: Getty

Spurs, who picked up their first win days before, were the better side throughout and scored via a Mike Penders own goal and Mathys Tel.

Chelsea had not lost to the north Londoners at their Stamford Bridge home in the Premier League since 2018.

Fans have become accustomed to beating Spurs, so Saturday's result came as a real shock.



A couple of supporters in particular were livid with the performance and made it clear to Colwill at full-time in a video on social media.

Chelsea fans clash with Colwill

As the centre-back applauded towards the West Lower, one fan was heard shouting: "Colwill, don't you f****** clap!"



"F*** off!" a furious second added, before crying out: "Shame on you!"

Colwill was led away by Danny Welbeck, before completing his round of applause to the Matthew Harding and East stands.



Chelsea were dealt a blow ahead of kick-off as Joao Pedro missed out on the squad.

The striker picked up an injury during training on Friday, according to manager Xabi Alonso.

Geovany Quenda was chosen over Danny Welbeck to join Palmer and Morgan Rogers in attack.

WARNING: STRONG LANGUAGE

2 Colwill was on the receiving end of fury from Chelsea fans in the West Lower as he applauded them Credit: Getty



Penders started in goal for the hosts as Emi Martinez remains out of action following jaw surgery.

The Argentina international was knocked out cold during the 2-0 win at Everton last weekend.

Chelsea are fourth in the Premier League, but could drop out of the top four by the end of Sunday.

They will travel to Liverpool on Wednesday night for a Carabao Cup last 16 clash, live on talkSPORT.



However, Chelsea then host Manchester United in the league just two-and-half days later, a match that will also be live on talkSPORT.

A trip to Sunderland on November 8 caps off their schedule before the international break.

Sports.title: EFL promotion contenders sack manager just 11 games into season
Sports.content:
Sheffield Wednesday have sacked manager Henrik Pedersen after just 11 games in League One.

The Owls are sitting in eighth place but have lost their last two games, prompting the board to make a swift decision.

3 Pedersen was looking to get Wednesday back into the Championship Credit: Getty

They lost 2-0 to Notts County and 2-0 to Doncaster Rovers - but had been unbeaten since August 20.

Wednesday are just two points off the play-off places and seven off top-of-the-table Huddersfield.

Should they win their game in hand, they would be in the top six and four points behind the leaders.

However, the club confirmed Pedersen has been sacked in a statement on Sunday morning.

It read: "Sheffield Wednesday Football Club confirms that Henrik Pedersen has left the club with immediate effect.

"Henrik led the first team through an exceptional period in the club's history, providing stability and leadership during a time of significant uncertainty and change.

"The club would like to place on record its sincere thanks to Henrik for his contribution and wishes him every success in the future."

Sporting Director Simon Wilson said: "First and foremost, I want to thank Henrik for his professionalism, commitment and contribution during an exceptionally challenging period for Sheffield Wednesday.

“We knew the start of this season would be difficult due to the scale of change across the club, but our expectation was always that we would develop as the season progressed, establishing a recognisable style of play and greater consistency in our performances.

“Although we have accumulated points, we haven’t seen enough progress in those areas. We believe making a change now gives us the best opportunity to establish those foundations and build towards the second half of the season and beyond.

“We remain ambitious about what we can achieve this campaign, and our focus remains on building a Sheffield Wednesday team with a clear identity, capable of delivering sustained improvement and long-term success.”

Matt Hamshaw will take interim charge of the first team while the club undertakes the process of appointing its next head coach.

3 Pedersen joined the Owls in July 2025 and remained with them all last year Credit: Rex

Sheffield Wednesday's season so far

Wednesday have five wins, three draws and three defeats from their opening games so far.

Their victories include a 7-2 drubbing of Bromley and back-to-back away wins over Wycombe Wanderers and Peterborough United.

However, those back-to-back defeats against Notts County and Doncaster have cost Pedersen.

Speaking after the 2-0 defeat to Donny, he said: “I feel the anger like you feel the anger because we are not happy after a great result Saturday at home and then we have two lost in two games. Of course I feel the same anger.

“I’m hurting because it’s not who we want to be. We want to be a dominant team from the first to the last moment, not only a second half or period of the game.

"We we want to have higher standard through 90 minutes. It’s hurt me really that we miss something here, and yeah, this is what we want to work on to to increase very quickly.”

3 Wednesday will now look to gain promotion without Pedersen Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Pedersen's time at Wednesday

Pedersen was thrown into a club in disarray due to the previous owner.

Dejphon Chansiri consistently failed to pay tax bills and in the end, the club was taken off him.

They were put into administration and hit with a total of 18 points deducted and left with a squad that was hastily put together.

As a result, they won two Championship games all season.

There were 12 draws and 32 defeats across a year to forget for everyone connected with the club, bar Chansiri being forced out.

But after suffering through all of that, he's been sacked.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer’s poor record against big six exposed as Chelsea star called out
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer’s poor record against big six exposed as Chelsea star called out

Cole Palmer's pretty dreadful record against the so-called 'big six' has come to light after his red card in Chelsea's 2-0 defeat to Tottenham Hotspur.

Spurs sealed just their second Premier League win at Stamford Bridge on Saturday as a Mike Penders own goal and Mathys Tel won the game for Roberto De Zerbi's men.

3 Palmer's red card ended a poor game for the England international

Palmer received two yellow cards to be sent off, with the first one for an off-the-ball incident against Matheus Fernandes.

He was then late to a tackle with Conor Gallagher and picked up the second booking.

It also was another game in which he failed to score or assist against a fellow big six side.

And if you take away penalties, his end product in those matches has been very poor.

In 25 games, he has two non-penalty goals, and they are both against Manchester United.

Cole Palmer's record against 'big six' *Excluding penalties Man United - Played 6, Scored 2 Arsenal - Played 5, Scored 0 Liverpool - Played 3, Scored 0 Man City - Played 6, Scored 0 Tottenham - Played 5, Scored 0

Poor example

Despite his age, Palmer is one of the most experienced players in the team.

And talkSPORT presenter Max Scott feels Palmer should have been sent off for his first yellow card.

After a series of late tackles, including one by Fernandes on the England international, he reacted badly and charged at the Tottenham midfielder, who was on the floor.

He connected with his head and sparked a brawl, but the attacking midfielder was only booked.

On that incident, Scott said: "Cole Palmer was lucky not to be sent off for that yellow card he got on Matheus Fernandes.

"He's a lucky boy that he wasn't sent off earlier in that game because that is a naughty charge towards Fernandes, who is on the floor.

"Last week, [Yehor] Yarmoliuk was sent off for Brentford for a silly nudge with the head, but VAR should have looked at the Palmer incident because he's charged towards a player on the floor and chested him in the head.

"So, if it is about aggressive, violent conduct, then that was more of a red card than Yarmoliuk last week.

"Palmer needs to take a look at himself because he might be an absolutely wonderful player, but there are bubbling concerns about the attitude.

"He's let Chelsea down in a fixture you expect them to win, so it will be interesting to see how he bounces back."

3 It has been a mixed season for Palmer so far Credit: Getty

3 Palmer still has two goals and three assists in the Premier League so far this season Credit: Getty

Discipline issues

That was Palmer's first red card of his club career, though he can be prone to picking up yellows.

The 24-year-old looked stunned when he was sent off, but Scott isn't the only one who believes that Palmer was lucky not to be shown a straight red.

Speaking on Weekend Sports Breakfast, Katie Shanahan said: "I thought he should have had a red card for that first one where he had a yellow.

"But what was he doing? He is one of the best players in the team, arguably the best.

"Surely, he should be showing signs of leadership, maturity - this is not good, and he can't be doing it going forward because it costs the team."

And former Premier League striker Tony Cascarino believes that the versatile forward is prone to a few silly moments that can cost his team.

"I don't know him personally, but I don't consider him a leader. He is a performance player that wants the ball and can make things happen when he just plays his game.

"He is never captain material with the way he talks and plays the game.

"When he doesn't get his own way, he will start doing daft things, and he does.

"Palmer can lift players with a moment. He is capable of incredible moments, but if games are not going his way, he is going to do something petulant, and he's done it more than once."

Palmer will serve his suspension in the Carabao Cup fourth round match with Liverpool on Wednesday.

He will then be available for the Premier League clash with Man United at Stamford Bridge next Saturday.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick drops Man United captain Bruno Fernandes after critical comments
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes was dropped for Manchester United's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

The club captain has been criticised for his midweek post-match rant in which he took aim at their tactics in the 4-1 defeat to Como.

2 Fernandes was left out of the United team to face Bournemouth by Carrick after his public rant Credit: Getty

Fernandes publicly questioned the game plan from under-fire head coach Michael Carrick as United extended their winless run to seven.

With United in desperate need of a win, the Portuguese international was left out the starting XI to host Bournemouth.

It's the first Premier League match that will not see him appear from the off this season.

His 14 assists and 96 created chances is also the most of any player in Europe's top five leagues since Carrick's first match in January.

Fernandes trained on Friday and Saturday, and remained available for selection for the match.

He was still in the matchday squad, with Harry Maguire taking the armband, but was an unused substitute.

Carrick confirmed that his decision to drop Fernandes was for 'pure football' reasons.

What has Carrick said on Fernandes?

Speaking to Sky Sports ahead of Man United's game with Bournemouth, Carrick confirmed why he left out the captain.

“When you have options it’s always a difficult decision. We have to make the right one for today and the team to get that performance we want,” Carrick said.

When asked whether Fernandes had been dropped for football or other reasons, he responded: “Pure football.”

2 Carrick has chosen to leave his captain out of the starting XI for the crucial match Credit: Getty

United have just one league win from seven matches this season, and a goal difference of zero.

They are only a point above the bottom three as things stand, and defeat leaves them in a precarious position and likely spell the end of Carrick's tenure as the head coach.

Former Bournemouth and Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe is understood to be preferred by technical director Jason Wilcox if a change is made.

Wilcox also admires Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler, although he is not interested in the job.

Ex-Chelsea and Tottenham manager Antonio Conte would be open to taking over, but has insisted that he is not in talks with any club.

Sports.title: This was the end for Michael Carrick after his gang of the damned were relentlessly dismantled 3-0 by Bournemouth... he will be the next to walk into Man United's endless winter, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
This was the end for Michael Carrick after his gang of the damned were relentlessly dismantled 3-0 by Bournemouth... he will be the next to walk into Man United's endless winter, writes OLIVER HOLT

The yellowed leaves fell from the trees and danced and skittered across the forecourt at Old Trafford. Squalls battered the old stadium and Manchester United supporters bowed their heads into the winds of Storm Boelo. These are the rites of autumn and, in this part of the city, they double as prophecies of deaths foretold.

In the great churn of unfortunates who have occupied the manager’s position at United since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in May 2013, October, November and December is the favoured sacking season. Jose Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Erik ten Hag have all met their fates as the branches have been stripped bare.

Now, it was Michael Carrick’s turn. This was the end for him. There can be little doubt about that. The United boss, a favourite son of the fans here when he was a player, a decent, modest, self-effacing man, stood on the touchline in a coat of funereal black, his arms folded in front of him, his face set in a desperate grimace as he watched his gang of the damned being relentlessly dismantled by Bournemouth.

It was hard to watch, just as it had been hard to watch United humiliated by Como in the Champions League last week. The truth was obvious: this United is a rabble, a loose collection of over-entitled, overpaid, over-promoted and overdone losers who have done their bit to throw their boss under the bus.

It is easy to say but the way some of them played against Marco Rose’s intelligent, well-drilled, energetic team, they do not deserve to wear the United shirt. They are not fit for it. They are an embarrassment to it. This comprehensive 3-0 defeat left them in 16th place in the Premier League, one point above the relegation zone. It is where they deserve to be.

Carrick cannot survive this and, particularly, he cannot survive the manner of recent defeats. This was the end for him and it ought to be the end for some of the hapless club apparatchiks who let him down in the summer with their hopeless recruitment in the transfer window.

Manchester United were hammered 3-0 at home by Bournemouth on another dismal day

The damaging defeat leaves Red Devils boss Michael Carrick on the brink of losing his job

The club is in chaos, on and off the field. Bruno Fernandes, the club captain, was dropped after criticising Carrick in midweek. Lisandro Martinez, who was disciplined for criticising the club’s owners, did return against Bournemouth but only in the second half. He is a liability anyway.

This is not all on Carrick, though. In fact, in the list of those responsible for this shambles, he is low on the list. The Glazers, who have pillaged the club, are top of the list. Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the minority owner, who has overseen the descent into this mayhem, is next.

This is a club riven by dissent from top to bottom, a club that has declared war on its most loyal supporters by trying to accelerate the move away from season ticket holders towards tourists and day-trippers because money is king for this regime and season-ticket holders do not spend enough on match days.

It was little wonder that, as Bournemouth scored goal after goal, the supporters turned their ire on the owners and their much-trumpeted plans for a move away from Old Trafford. How empty and futile those plans seem when the club is in this state. ‘You can stick your new stadium up your arse,’ the Stretford End sang.

And so Carrick stood there in that black coat, arms folded, taking the brickbats. ‘You’re getting sacked in the morning,’ the Bournemouth fans yelled at him. Carrick and United are easy meat. ‘You’re going down with the City,’ they chanted delightedly as United melted away in front of them.

The first drama of the day had come before kick-off with the publication of the United teamsheet. It showed that Fernandes, the club captain and the man who has carried the team through many of the lean years at Old Trafford, had been dropped. Harry Maguire was named as skipper in his stead.

After his criticism of Carrick’s tactics following the humiliating Champions League defeat to Como last week, it was hardly a surprise that Fernandes paid the penalty. Carrick would have looked weak if he had started him. Carrick may be standing on a burning deck but he was still trying to reassert his authority amid the flames.

The chants against the Glazers and Ratcliffe started soon after kick-off. So did the Bournemouth chances. Rayan headed just wide from Bournemouth’s first corner and burst through on a breakaway only to drive his shot straight at a defender as United retreated in disarray.

Bournemouth were superb, yet United were woeful and another manager looks set to leave

The defeat leaves United just above the relegation zone with seven points from eight games

United's fans turned on the club's hierarchy as Bournemouth extended their lead (pictured - CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox), but continued to support Carrick

Bournemouth failed to capitalise as the opportunities kept coming. When Marcus Tavernier escaped yet again down the left wing, he drove his cross straight into the arms of Senne Lammens but as United’s defenders remonstrated with each other, the Stretford End lost its patience and roared out its dismay at what was happening.

Ayden Heaven was lucky to escape with a yellow card for launching himself into the air and into a double-footed tackle that Evanilson skipped out of rather than risk serious injury. Then, from the resulting free kick eight minutes before half-time, Bournemouth took the lead that their play had deserved.

Justin Kluivert swung the ball to the back post and sailed over the massed ranks of the United defence to where Rayan was ghosting in. Rayan was unmarked. He met the ball on the volley with his left foot and rammed it past Lammens. United tried to complain about a foul but they had no grounds.

Five minutes later, Bournemouth doubled their lead. Leny Yoro slipped under pressure on the right side of the United box and Adrien Truffert pounced on the mistake and squared the ball to Tavernier. Tavernier completed the formalities, turning the ball past Lammens from close range.

Old Trafford erupted in a fusillade of boos. A black flag was lowered from the back of the first tier of the Stretford End that said, in red letters, ‘Standards’. The outline of the faces of Roy Keane, Eric Cantona and Bryan Robson were below it, symbols of better times and better players. ‘You’re getting sacked in the morning,’ the Bournemouth fans sang at Carrick.

United were dire. Djordje Petrovic did save well from Bryan Mbeumo just before the interval but it was a rare moment of threat. There were more groans from the crowd when Mason Mount’s corner failed miserably to clear the first defender. It was another symbol of a miserable half for the home team.

Things were still not bad enough to prompt Carrick to call on Fernandes. Maybe nothing would have been. He did bring Matheus Cunha on for Youri Tielemans but Evanilson had a goal disallowed for offside seconds after the restart. Bournemouth should have been three up a couple of minutes later. Rayan, one-on-one with Lammens, hit the ball too close to the goalkeeper.

But United barely posed a threat. They hardly ever do. In seven of their 11 games this season United have failed to score more than once. United have only 10 goals in eight league outings now. They are toothless as well as gutless.

Carrick dropped Bruno Fernandes for the match and then left him on the bench throughout

Bournemouth were superb as they capped off one of the best weeks in the club's history

Bournemouth should have won by more but their third was a beauty. Twenty minutes from time, Lewis Cook played a ball down the line and Lammens hurtled out of his goal in a doomed attempt to try to get to it first.

Evanilson got to it first, took it round the goalkeeper and clipped the ball brilliantly into the empty goal from a tight angle. United’s humiliation was almost complete. In the dying minutes, the United fans chanted abuse at Ratcliffe’s henchmen Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and Omar Berrada, the chief executive.

But everyone knows that it will not be them who pay the price. In autumn’s parade of the damned, Carrick will be the next to walk into Manchester United’s endless winter.
