World.title: 2027: VON’s Ex-DG warns against ethnic tension fuelled by disregard for presidential zoning
World.content:
Former Director-General of the Voice of Nigeria (VON) and APC foundation member, Osita Okechukwu, has said that former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s breach of zoning is fuelling political tensions in the North and, by extension, nationwide, thereby vindicating advocates of Nigeria’s power-rotation and zoning convention.

Mr Okechukwu, who said this in a statement on Sunday in Abuja, appealed to northerners to avoid the dangers of ethno-identity politics driven by one man and his cohorts, noting that countries like Sudan have yet to recover from ethnic rivalry.

“The South has other presidential candidates, and truly Atiku and Tinubu are ten and ten pence going by their antecedents,” he said.

He lamented that the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) is yet to recover from Atiku’s breach of zoning in the 2023 presidential election, contending that the 2027 contest would have been less acrimonious if the African Democratic Congress (ADC) had respected the principle of presidential power rotation and presented a southern candidate.

Mr Okechukwu reminded Nigerians that some prominent politicians, including Abubakar Rimi, Umaru Shinkafi, Adamu Ciroma, Olusola Saraki, Alex Ekwueme, and Ogbonnaya Onu, whom he described as patriots, saved the country in 1999 from ethno-identity politics by subordinating their personal presidential ambitions to broader national unity.

“Zoning advocates have consistently maintained that presidential power rotation is a vital instrument for managing Nigeria’s diversity.

“The current political tension demonstrates why zoning convention should not be treated as an expendable item, merely to accommodate an individual’s presidential ambition. Moreover, when he has no concrete solution to our economic quagmire,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The former VON DG cited the peaceful nature of the 1999, 2007 and 2019 presidential elections of Olusegun Obasanjo vs Olu Falae, Muhammadu Buhari vs Umaru Yar’Adua and Muhammadu Buhari vs Atiku Abubakar, all living testimony of how rotation convention undoubtedly sustained national balance.

He expressed concern over reports that security personnel are deployed to protect campaign posters and billboards of presidential candidates, describing the situation as a troubling development.

He noted the high opportunity cost of deploying security officials to political duties when there are myriads of kidnappings, armed robberies, the farmer-herder crisis, and sundry insurgencies unattended.

Mr Okechukwu, therefore, called on Atiku’s supporters and other political stakeholders “to stop framing the 2027 presidential contest as a zero-sum game between North and South; such rhetoric could deepen ethnic divisions and may inadvertently place our fledgling democracy in harm’s way.”

World.title: From Garden to Market: How women’s vegetable farming is transforming household livelihoods in Kaduna
World.content:
Asabe Daniel grew up watching her father working on his farms.

But after losing her job with the Soba Local Government three years ago, farming became more than a family tradition for her. It became a way to survive.

A resident of Wusasa village in Zaria Local Government Area of Kaduna State, Ms Daniel now combines vegetable farming with making masa, a baked rice breakfast delicacy mostly eaten in many northern states, to support herself.

She cultivates soya beans and tomatoes on a small piece of land.

Speaking with PREMIUM TIMES, Ms Daniel said she learnt the basics of farming from her father but had to deepen her knowledge after turning to agriculture to achieve financial independence.

“I get my tomato seeds from neighbours who, after washing their tomatoes, I request water or seeds, and from there I nurse them till they reach the stage of transplanting,” she said.

“Although I started it three years ago to gain financial independence, tomato farming became more profitable because I get to feed from it and sell.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Her experience reflects a growing reality among women in Kaduna’s rural communities, where small vegetable farms are increasingly becoming sources of food, income and household stability.

‘I want to turn tomatoes into tin tomatoes’

Ms Daniel dreams of expanding her tomato farm and processing the produce into packaged tomato products.

But a familiar obstacle stands in the way: a lack of capital.

She needs money to buy seeds, fertiliser and other farm inputs, as well as secure additional land for cultivation.

She described access to land as one of her biggest challenges. She pays to use the small piece of land she currently cultivates.

Her story illustrates a major barrier facing women farmers in Nigeria: while agriculture provides an important source of livelihood, women often struggle to access the resources needed to expand.

Land, finance, technology and other productive resources remain difficult for many women to obtain, particularly in communities where traditional norms often favour men in ownership and control of agricultural assets.

‘My husband encouraged me’

For Halima Yusuf, her husband encouraged her to start vegetable farming.

A full-time housewife for about 10 years after marriage, Ms Yusuf said her husband, who sells chickens and chicken feed, encouraged her to start farming so she could have a source of income.

This is her second year of farming.

“Last year I cultivated soya beans, and with the help of my husband, who bought the piece of land for me, I was able to get three bags,” she said.

“This year I am practising relay farming where on the same piece of land I planted chilli pepper and onions.”

Unlike some of the other women interviewed, Ms Yusuf said she has not encountered major challenges as a woman farmer because her husband has provided the support she needs.

But for others, limited access to land and capital nearly kept them from farming altogether.

Seeds that changed Maria’s story

Maria Kabiru, a mother of three from Bomo village in Sabon Gari Local Government Area, had always been interested in farming.

But lack of money and land discouraged her from taking the first step.

Her situation changed when the East-West Seed Foundation, through its Deliver Nigeria project, provided her with cabbage and onion seeds and trained her in improved vegetable farming techniques.

Ms Kabiru started with cabbage during the dry season, then moved to onions.

She cultivated the crops on a small piece of land in front of her house, with her husband helping her to water the farm using water from their well and a nearby river.

But starting was not easy.

“I used my own money to buy seeds to start the cabbage farm, and when I started, many women in my area tried to discourage me, especially here in the North where women feel farming is an activity done by men who must provide for their families, not an activity that a woman could engage in,” she said.

Despite the discouragement, the farm thrived.

“My cabbage plantation did well because my husband helped me to nurture the farm, and I got a lot of money from selling the cabbage right on the farm,” she said.

The success encouraged Ms Kabiru to go beyond her own farm.

She created a group of women farmers in Bomo, where she now teaches improved vegetable farming techniques she learned through the foundation.

‘I am now among the biggest okra sellers’

For Mariya Nasiru-Ibrahim, okra farming has become a profitable enterprise.

She said okra farming has improved her financial situation to the point that she is now one of the biggest okra sellers in her village.

But her ambition is now limited by the size of the land available to her.

She wants to acquire a bigger farm so she can expand her cultivation using improved seeds.

Her experience mirrors that of several other women whose farms have become profitable but whose ability to grow their businesses remains constrained by access to land and other inputs.

‘Vegetable farming has changed my life’

In Koraye village, Fatima Mohammed said vegetable farming has become her main source of income.

She began farming after completing her national youth service programme and failing to secure a job.

Her brother, who now lives in Saudi Arabia, provided her with capital. At the same time, her friend, Isma’il Danladi, a farmer, taught her how to cultivate onions during both wet and dry seasons.

“This year would be my fifth year of farming onions during wet and dry seasons, and I have not regretted my actions because vegetable farming has provided a job that helps feed myself and my mother,” she said.

For Ms Mohammed, the dry season provides the greatest financial opportunity.

“I gain more money with onions during the dry season because that’s when it becomes expensive, and few farmers cultivate it during the dry season,” she said.

But water remains a major challenge.

She said insufficient water during the dry season affects the quality of the onions she produces.

‘Carrots also improved my household nutrition’

For Hannatu Adamu, vegetable farming benefits go beyond income.

Ms Adamu, who has cultivated carrots for five years, said the crop has improved her household’s nutrition while also giving her greater financial independence.

She recalled how her youngest child suffered from malnutrition at nine months old.

“I remember when my last-born was just nine months old, he suffered from malnutrition and I was advised to boil carrots, rice, egg and make it into a smoothie to improve his diet,” she said.

But like other farmers, she faces rising input costs.

She identified fertiliser and seeds as some of her greatest difficulties and called on the government to subsidise farming inputs to help lift farmers out of poverty.

Fertiliser support

Women farmers are among the key beneficiaries of the Governor Uba Sani administration’s latest free fertiliser distribution, an intervention aimed at reducing production costs and strengthening the capacity of smallholder farmers.

The programme, which began with the distribution of 500 truckloads of fertiliser and the deployment of tractors, targets 150,000 smallholder farmers across the state’s 23 local government areas.

Speaking to PREMIUM TIMES at the Babban Dodo fertiliser redemption centre in Zaria Local Government Area, the Supervisory Councillor for Agriculture and Forestry, Nuhu Dogara-Malami, said it was the third consecutive year of the administration’s fertiliser intervention programme, with particular attention being paid to women and young farmers.

He said rising input costs had made it difficult for smallholder farmers to maintain or expand production.

At the redemption centre, women beneficiaries welcomed the intervention, describing it as timely support as fertiliser and other farm inputs became increasingly unaffordable.

Amina Suleiman, who cultivates maize, rice and beans, said it was the first time she had benefited from a government agricultural intervention. In contrast, Masa’uda Aliyu said the support made her feel that her efforts as a farmer were being recognised.

Hadiza Ibrahim, who grows tomatoes in her backyard while her husband cultivates maize, said the fertiliser would benefit both of them.

“I use the fertiliser for my tomatoes, while my husband will also use it on his maize farm,” she said.

Other beneficiaries, including Husaina Musa from Dogarawa and cabbage farmer Ashiru Mohammed from Muchia, also thanked the government, with Mr Mohammed saying the support could help increase his output as high input costs continue to burden small-scale farmers.

How institutions are supporting women farmers

Beyond individual efforts, agricultural extension workers and development organisations are helping women to acquire improved farming knowledge.

Sani Inusa, an agricultural engineer and rural agriculture developer with the National Agricultural Extension and Research Liaison Services (NAERLS) at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, said his organisation works with numerous women’s groups in Zaria, Giwa and Sabon Gari local government areas.

The training covers improved methods of cultivating vegetables, rearing animals and starting small-scale businesses.

Mr Inusa said agricultural workers have visited rural communities for about 15 years to train women to cultivate vegetables, rice and maize.

They also provide seeds and fertiliser, particularly before the rainy season.

“There has been an increase in women’s groups both in size and work,” he saidid, adding that Zaria Local Government alone has more than 30 women’s groups, with between 25 and 50 women in each group.

The groups are also exposed to health education and climate-smart agriculture.

According to Mr Inusa, the women are taught how to identify suitable crops for their land and determine what to grow to maximise profit.

They are also trained in pest control, including which chemicals to use, when to plant to reduce pest attacks, and how to minimise chemical use so their produce remains largely organic.

The extension gap

Despite these efforts, Mr Inusa said a major gap remains between agricultural extension workers and farmers in Kaduna State.

He said many local government areas have extension workers who do not actively reach farmers, leaving rural communities without access to up-to-date agricultural knowledge.

“The gap could be closed when the extension workers endeavour to meet these farmers and teach them new techniques in farming,” he said.

He also advised local governments to register women farmers’ groups.

Such registration, he said, could make it easier for the women to access loans, farm inputs and other forms of agricultural support.

Why women farmers matter: Women’s growing involvement in vegetable farming is significant in Kaduna State, where agriculture remains a major source of livelihood.

Kaduna’s Agricultural Development Agency estimates that the state has about 1.3 million farming households, while agriculture contributes about 38 per cent to the state’s Gross Domestic Product.

Women are involved in crop production, livestock, processing and marketing.

Yet they often face greater difficulties accessing land, credit, extension services and farm inputs.

Kaduna State’s Women’s Economic Empowerment Policy says only 4.7 per cent of women in the state independently own agricultural land, while 92.7 per cent do not own land.

The policy identifies limited access to productive resources as a major constraint to women’s participation in agriculture.

Studies of women farmers in Kaduna have similarly identified high input costs, inadequate capital, limited extension services and gender-related barriers as obstacles to increased productivity.

For women operating small farms or cultivating food crops around their homes, access to fertiliser, seeds and other inputs can therefore directly affect how much they produce and the income available to their families.

Kaduna government’s intervention

The Kaduna State Government has also identified women’s participation in agriculture as part of its broader economic empowerment agenda.

The Ministry of Business, Innovation and Technology, working with the Ministry of Agriculture and Dev-Afrique Advisors, has helped to advance the agricultural component of the state’s Women’s Economic Empowerment Policy.

At a strategic session on the policy, agriculture commissioner Murtala Dabo outlined initiatives to improve women’s access to arable land.

Mr Dabo said women’s participation in agriculture matters not only from an equality perspective but also for the state’s economic development.

“Women’s participation in agriculture is not merely about equity—it’s essential to our economic development,” he said.

He said women, from labourers to small-scale farmers and entrepreneurs, must be positioned to contribute to and benefit from Kaduna’s agricultural economy.

The strategic discussions also examined sector-specific interventions that could support women-led agricultural enterprises and strengthen their participation across the agricultural value chain.

From survival to enterprise. These women’s stories show that vegetable farming is increasingly more than a subsistence activity.

For Asabe Daniel, it provided a livelihood after she lost her job.

For Maria Kabiru, access to seeds and training opened a new income source and eventually inspired her to train other women.

For Fatima Mohammed, onion farming became a job after she struggled to secure employment.

For Hannatu Adamu, carrot farming has helped both her finances and her family’s nutrition.

And for Halima Yusuf, farming provided an opportunity to become economically active after years as a full-time housewife.

But their experiences also reveal the limits of what individual determination can achieve.

Land remains difficult to access. Fertiliser and seeds are expensive. Water is scarce during the dry season. Capital is limited, while agricultural extension services do not always reach the farmers who need them.

For these women, the next stage is not simply to keep farming; it is to expand.

To move from small plots to larger farms.

From selling fresh produce to processing.

From individual efforts to organised women’s farming groups.

And from household survival to sustainable agricultural enterprises.

Women have already shown what they can achieve with limited resources.

The question remains whether institutions, governments and agricultural support programmes can provide the land, finance, inputs, technology and knowledge needed to turn those small farms into sustainable businesses.

For women like Asabe, Maria, Fatima and Hannatu, vegetable farming has already changed what a small piece of land means.

World.title: Death toll in Taraba terror attack rises to 40
World.content:
The number of people killed in the 23 October terror attack on Binnari village in Karim Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State has risen to 40.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the police in the state confirmed that 10 locals were killed in the attack.

Victor Mshelizah, the spokesperson for Taraba police command, said police operatives were deployed to restore order in the area.

However, Amnesty International Nigeria reported that 40 people were killed in the attack, adding that additional bodies were being discovered.

Other sources reported higher figures, with many people still missing.

Locals told this newspaper that houses, shops and goods were razed by the armed men who infiltrated the community through a border community in Plateau State.

“The attack which took place on Friday 23 October 2026 shows utter disdain for the sanctity of life,” Amnesty said, calling for an impartial investigation and justice for the victims.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It corroborated locals’ accounts of the assailants burning foodstuffs, homes, shops and motorcycles.

“The community is now littered with dead bodies, some burnt beyond recognition, as families declare many still missing,” Amnesty said.

Amnesty International accused Nigerian authorities of failing to adequately protect rural communities from repeated attacks.

READ ALSO: 10 killed in Taraba attack as residents flee community

“The Nigerian authorities continue to leave rural communities in some parts of the north at the mercy of gunmen who repeatedly commit atrocities with impunity,” the organisation said.

It called for an impartial investigation into the attack and adequate reparations for survivors.

“On the side of the authorities, issuing bland statements condemning these horrific attacks is not enough,” Amnesty said. “Genuine commitment to protecting the people must be demonstrated by ensuring adequate security of lives and property, as well as ensuring justice for the victims.”

The organisation added that the failure to prosecute suspected perpetrators was encouraging further violence.

“Consistent failure of the authorities to bring the suspected perpetrators to justice is clearly emboldening impunity,” it said.

Taraba is mapped to the insurgency-ravaged North-east, but it has suffered more from banditry, farmer-herder crises and communal clashes, just like its neighbouring state, Plateau.

World.title: Is Wizkid failing his fans in 2026?
World.content:
Wizkid

By Ayo Onikoyi

It appears music powerhouse Ayodeji Balogun is keeping his fans hanging too long on a thread after he made a promise of his seventh solo studio album “coming soon” in June 2026. Three months down the line, the wait continues without any actual date in sight.

The Wizkid FC, his fanatical fans, wouldn’t throw any tantrum about this, but the question has to be asked as to what is keeping the “Holla at Ya Boy” star from unleashing his “Sexy” (title of his seventh studio album) on the music scene.

The fact that the superstar started 2026 on the up and up hasn’t helped matters because it felt pretty much like he gave his fans a shot in the arm and left them high and dry.

He began the year with ‘Jogodo’, a collaboration with Asake that set the stage for their joint extended play, ‘REAL, Vol. 1’. He subsequently expanded his catalogue with releases involving Latin music, British R&B and other contemporary sounds, reinforcing his reputation as an artiste comfortable working across musical boundaries.

One of the defining moments of his 2026 output was the January release of ‘REAL, Vol. 1’, a four-track EP with Asake. Released on January 23, the project brought together two generations of Nigerian music stars whose styles have helped shape the contemporary Afrobeats sound.

The project followed the success of their earlier collaborations, including ‘MMS’ on Asake’s 2024 album, ‘Lungu Boy’. It featured songs such as ‘Jogodo’, ‘Iskolodo’ and ‘Turbulence’, combining infectious rhythms, melodic hooks and elements of contemporary African dance music.

‘Jogodo’, released ahead of the EP in January, served as the lead single and generated anticipation for the full project. The collaboration offered fans an opportunity to hear the two singers build on their established musical chemistry.

The singer continued this international run with ‘Alive’, a collaboration with British singer-songwriter Jorja Smith, released on July 2. The song blended R&B and Afrobeats, with production by P2J, and appeared ahead of Smith’s third studio album, ‘What Are The Odds’.

Another notable release was ‘Coca Body’, featuring Dutch rapper and singer Frenna, British-Nigerian singer Odeal and Wizkid. Released in July, the song brought together the artistes’ melodic approaches in a record that drew on Afrobeats, R&B and hip-hop influences.

These collaborations highlighted Wizkid’s continued willingness to explore different sounds while maintaining the relaxed vocal delivery that has become a hallmark of his music.

Beyond his recorded collaborative outputs, his fans still await his next solo effort. In June, he unveiled ‘Sexy’ as the title of his seventh studio album at a listening party in Paris. However, a release date and full tracklist had not been announced at the time of the report.

World.title: FG disburses ₦39bn to tertiary institutions
World.content:
Dr Tunji Alausa, Minister of Education

Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The Federal Government has disbursed the sum of ₦38.93 billion to 166 public tertiary institutions, nationwide, under the Needs Assessment Revitalisation Fund.

Details of the disbursement contained in a statement by the Head, Media Unit of the Federal Ministry of Finance, Efe Ovuakporie in Abuja, yesterday, showed that beneficiaries included 79 universities, 46 polytechnics and 41 colleges of education.

The funds would support approved projects aimed at addressing infrastructure gaps and improving teaching and learning facilities across the institutions.

The university component accounts for ₦28.5 billion for 79 institutions, while 46 polytechnics have allocations totalling ₦5.8 billion. The 41 colleges of education received ₦4.7 billion.

The statement read in part, “The intervention forms part of the Federal Government’s efforts to address the needs of public universities and support the implementation of agreed measures under the Memorandum of Understanding between the Federal Government and the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU).

“The funds are expected to enable beneficiary institutions to commence or advance approved projects addressing critical infrastructure and other identified institutional needs, with the overall objective of strengthening the quality of tertiary education in Nigeria.

The disbursement underscores the importance of effective coordination between the Federal Ministry of Finance, the Federal Ministry of Education and beneficiary institutions in ensuring that approved public funding translates into tangible improvements in educational infrastructure and institutional capacity.”

World.title: Igbo must unite, build alliances to produce president — Soludo
World.content:
Governor Soludo

…Opens up on inclusion in APC presidential campaign council

…Says Igbo identity no reason to back Obi

…Declares victory over Monday sit-at-home, says Anambra back to life

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has said the Igbo must unite and build strategic alliances across Nigeria to stand a chance of producing the country’s president.

Soludo said the South-East must overcome political divisions and forge strategic alliances with other regions to strengthen its bargaining power.

He cited the alliance-building approach associated with First Republic political leader, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, arguing that the Igbo needed a broader national support base to realise their presidential ambition.

He also pointed to President Bola Tinubu’s political alliances as an example of the importance of coalition-building in securing power.

Gov. Soludo who spoke exclusively with Vanguard, declared that he and the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) would support President Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, explaining why he accepted an appointment in the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council despite belonging to another party.

The Governor said APGA’s leadership had collectively adopted Tinubu for a second term and resolved not to field a presidential candidate, adding that the decision was consistent with the party’s tradition of supporting presidents irrespective of their political platforms.

He recalled that former Anambra governors Peter Obi and Willie Obiano had similarly supported presidential candidates from other parties.

Speaking through his Chief Press Secretary, Mr Christian Aburime, Gov. Soludo said he had since, communicated APGA’s position to President Tinubu during the President’s visit to Anambra to inaugurate landmark projects, including the Government House, Solution Fun City and roads.

Obi’s Igbo identity no reason to back him

On expectations that Soludo should support his predecessor and the presidential flag bearer of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, Aburime said the two politicians belonged to different parties and did not share the same political ideology.

He acknowledged that Obi was qualified to contest the presidency but maintained that shared ethnicity should not determine political support.

“Politics shouldn’t be based on emotion or sentiment. They have different ideologies,” he said, insisting that Nigerians should support parties based on their capacity to improve citizens’ lives rather than ethnic or regional considerations.

Aburime also dismissed the assumption that Anambra voters would repeat their overwhelming support for Obi in 2023, declaring that the political dynamics had changed.

“2023 is gone. 2027 is not going to be 2023,” he said, expressing confidence that APGA members would vote for Tinubu.

Defends Tinubu’s economic reforms

On the removal of fuel subsidy and foreign exchange reforms, Aburime said Soludo supported Tinubu’s economic policies, describing them as painful but necessary measures to address longstanding structural weaknesses.

He argued that the previous practice of printing money to sustain the economy was unsustainable, adding that the reforms would eventually yield benefits.

On whether Tinubu had influenced former President Muhammadu Buhari to adopt better economic policies, Aburime said it was impossible to know whether the President had offered such advice behind the scenes, noting that influence did not guarantee acceptance.

Kanu’s release will be resolved politically

On the continued detention of Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) leader, Nnamdi Kanu, Aburime said the matter had assumed a political dimension and would ultimately require a political resolution.

Soludo had previously visited Kanu in detention and pledged to work towards securing his release.

Asked why the governor had yet to achieve that objective despite his closeness and relationship with Tinubu, Aburime declined to comment extensively but said efforts towards a resolution were not over.

“The Nnamdi Kanu case has become a political case and it will be resolved politically,” he said.

Monday sit-at-home defeated, Anambra back to life

Soludo declared that the enforcement of the Monday sit-at-home order by armed groups had been defeated, with commercial and social activities returning to normal across Anambra.

He said vehicles were moving freely and major centres, including Awka, Onitsha and Nnewi were bustling with activities.

“The war has been conquered, and all the debris is buried,” he said, insisting that residents could now move around freely and that Anambra was back to life.

END

World.title: Carrick unsure over Man Utd future after Bournemouth loss
World.content:
Manchester United’s English head coach Michael Carrick reacts to their defeat on the pitch after the English Premier League football match between Manchester United and Bournemouth at Old Trafford in Manchester, north west England, on October 25, 2026. Bournemouth won the game 3-0. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE. No use with unauthorized audio, video, data, fixture lists, club/league logos or ‘live’ services. Michael Carrick said he will do what is best for Manchester United after a 3-0 demolition by Bournemouth plunged his future as manager into doubt on Sunday.

Winless in eight games in all competitions, the 20-time English champions slipped to within one point of the relegation zone after a damaging defeat at Old Trafford.

“It’s a tough situation,” Carrick told Sky Sports. “What is next? I don’t know.

“I’ll always do what’s best for this football club. I’ve said it all along, I don’t change that now. I love what I do. I love the responsibility, but we’ll have to wait and see.”

Despite a dismal run of results, the United fans largely supported Carrick as he made his way off the field at full-time before they turned on the club’s players.

“I have mixed emotions to have that connection with the supporters in the moment we’re in. I need time to digest that,” added Carrick.

“I appreciate their support but the situation is where it’s at. We haven’t been good enough.”

Carrick’s decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench and not even introduce the Portuguese international as a substitute backfired.

Fernandes, last season’s Premier League player of the year, had criticised Carrick’s tactics after a 4-1 thrashing by Como on Wednesday.

“There’s always times in games when you are trying to change the course of the game and to make a difference,” said Carrick as he swerved questions on Fernandes’s absence. “Those were the decisions we made today.”

World.title: Igboho seeks wider security role for traditional rulers
World.content:
…unveils 20,000 Iru Ekun volunteers in Oyo

…links Abuja trip to strengthening regional security network

By Adeola Badru

Yoruba nation activist, Chief Sunday Adeyemo, popularly known as Sunday Igboho, has called for a stronger security role for traditional rulers across the South-West, declaring that the Iru Ekun Security Network, which he described as the brainchild of the region’s traditional institutions, has attracted 20,000 volunteers in Oyo State.

Igboho made the declaration on Sunday at the launch of the network at the popular Mapo Hall in Ibadan, where he explained that his recent visit to Abuja was aimed at strengthening the organisation’s security responsibilities and expanding its effectiveness in protecting communities.

The development was on the heels of the persistent security concerns across Nigeria, including abductions, killings and other criminal activities, which have placed renewed emphasis on cooperation between traditional institutions, local communities and conventional security agencies.

According to a statement issued by Igboho’s media office, no fewer than 20,000 volunteers joined the organisation in Oyo State, with its operational reach extending across Yorubaland and parts of Kwara and Niger states.

The statement said the Oyo launch followed similar inaugurations in Osun, Ekiti, Lagos, Ogun and Ondo states, alongside engagements with traditional rulers and community leaders.

It added that the organisation had collaborated with the Nigerian Army, the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies to tackle abductions, killings and other forms of insecurity, particularly in the South-West.

Commending the turnout at the Ibadan launch, Igboho said the participation of the volunteers demonstrated the willingness of residents to contribute to the safety of their communities, regardless of ethnic, religious or political differences.

“The impressive development represents a milestone which indicates genuine interest of Oyo people in active participation to ensure safety and security of residents, irrespective of tribes, religion and political affiliations,” he said.

Explaining the purpose of his Abuja trip, Igboho said the engagement was aimed at advancing the responsibilities of the security network, which he maintained was established through the initiative of traditional rulers in the South-West.

“I was in Abuja this morning so that Iru Ekun’s security responsibilities can be further strengthened.“

“This is because Iru Ekun is the brain child of South West traditional rulers and it will continue to serve its purpose for the peace and effective security of our communities,” he said.

He disclosed that the trip followed an invitation he received the previous night and linked the engagement to his collaboration with the Olubadan of Ibadanland.

“I received the call last night to come to Abuja. My Abuja trip was as a result of the collaboration with our traditional ruler, the Olubadan of Ibadanland,” he stated.

Igboho also expressed gratitude to God for what he described as protection against banditry, while acknowledging the contributions of traditional rulers to peace and security across the country.

“Firstly I want to thank Almighty God who has all powers, owns us, preserves us. The God that says we won’t be overcomed by bandits. We thank God,” he said.

He added: “After that, we thank all traditional rulers in Nigeria and may God grant them a long life.”

The activist subsequently commended President Bola Tinubu, whom he credited with providing a platform for members of the initiative to interact and pursue their security objectives.

“We are also paying homage to the person, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who provided this platform so that we can interact as Iru Ekun members,” he said.

Addressing the volunteers, Igboho expressed concern over what he described as the contemptuous attitude of some people towards them, predicting that their efforts would eventually attract recognition.

“Some people are still taking a despicable look at you (Volunteers). Soon they will lobby you for positions,” he remarked.

Meanwhile, Igboho urged Nigerians, including members of the Iru Ekun Security Network, to support Tinubu’s re-election bid and vote for the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the forthcoming January presidential election.

World.title: Isak extends hot streak as Liverpool sink Brighton
World.content:
Alexander Isak extended his hot streak in Liverpool’s 2-0 win against Brighton on Sunday as Reds boss Andoni Iraola savoured his first Premier League victory at Anfield.

Iraola’s side struck twice in quick succession in the first half, with Pascal Gross’s own goal followed by Isak’s latest strike.

Isak has netted six times in seven league games this season and has three goals in his last four matches.

After a turbulent debut season following his acrimonious move from Newcastle, the Sweden striker is finally beginning to repay his £125 million ($167 million) fee.

It was a welcome first taste of top-flight success at Anfield for Iraola, who had failed to win his first three league games on Merseyside since arriving from Bournemouth in the close season.

The Spaniard, who had won Champions League and League Cup games at Anfield, has led Liverpool to four successive victories in all competitions since the chastening 3-0 home defeat against Manchester City.

Liverpool have climbed to fourth place, just one point behind third-placed Brighton after inflicting the high-flying Seagulls’ second league loss this term.

The Reds are six points behind leaders City as they eye a potential title challenge.

Liverpool were winless in their previous five home league matches dating back to last season, drawing four times and losing once.

But they put Brighton to the sword in composed fashion, stopping the visitors’ recent goal blitz after they arrived at Anfield as the league’s top scorers.

Brighton should have taken an early lead when Diego Gomez’s pass caught out Virgil van Dijk and Gross crossed to Yasin Ayari, who fired wastefully over with the goal at his mercy.

– Rampant Reds –

Liverpool took full advantage of that escape to open the scoring in the 17th minute.

Ronald Araujo’s buccaneering run and cross into the Brighton area picked out Florian Wirtz for a powerful strike that took a hefty deflection off Gross as it whistled into the bottom corner.

Cody Gakpo nearly doubled Liverpool’s lead moments later with a rising drive that Bart Verbruggen tipped over.

Liverpool were rampant and it was no surprise when Isak bagged their second goal in the 21st minute.

Iraola opted for Bradley Barcola and Gakpo on the flanks despite Rio Ngumoha’s virtuoso performance in the midweek win against Villarreal.

And Barcola repaid that faith when he sprinted onto a long pass from Reds keeper Alisson Becker and guided a cross into Isak for a clinical close-range finish.

Isak has scored in three consecutive league appearances for the first time since January 2025 for Newcastle.

He was denied a fourth by Lewis Dunk’s last-ditch block after the Sweden striker took aim from Wirtz’s pass.

Liverpool kept pushing and Araujo’s blast forced a superb save from Verbruggen just before half-time.

The announcement that Liverpool’s troubled rivals Manchester United were losing to Bournemouth brought huge cheers from the Kop at the interval.

It was that kind of day for Liverpool, who comfortably held their lead in the second half despite losing Wirtz to an injury.

Iraola’s men are hitting their stride after an inconsistent start to the season.

Now come a pair of intriguing tests as Chelsea visit Anfield in the League Cup fourth round on Wednesday before second-placed Arsenal arrive for a crucial clash on November 1.

World.title: Man United’s misery continues, suffer 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth
World.content:
Bournemouth’s English midfielder #16 Marcus Tavernier celebrates after scoring their second goal during the English Premier League football match between Manchester United and Bournemouth at Old Trafford in Manchester, north west England, on October 25, 2026.
