World.title: Police: Signs of radicalization visible among younger teens
World.content:
Signs of radicalization are appearing in increasingly younger people and are already evident among 12- and 13-year-olds, said Pärtel Preinvalts, head of the radicalization prevention group at the Police and Border Guard Board's Northern Prefecture.

Preinvalts said the change in Estonia is not happening in isolation and can also be seen in other Western countries, including the United States.

"The age threshold is moving steadily downward in terms of young people's development. Whereas previously it was 15- and 16-year-olds, today it is 12- and 13-year-olds or even younger," Preinvalts said.

The number of violent crimes carried out by juveniles has risen over the last decade. There are fewer incidents such as shoplifting or vandalism and significantly more cases involving violence.

The proportion of juvenile crimes carried out against another person rose significantly from 2016 (27.5 percent) to 2022 (48.8 percent) Last year, the rate was recorded at 44.7 percent.

"Although the overall numbers may be falling, the proportion of crimes that have a much greater impact on victims and the community is increasing," Preinvalts said.

A sense of belonging

The head of the radicalization prevention group said young people often develop a sense of belonging through shared activities that may not initially appear to have anything to do with radicalization.

Many teenagers who join a group may not even realize what kind of gang they have joined until an adult explains it to them.

"Unfortunately, a recurring motive is so-called patriotism, which quite quickly turns into hatred," Preinvalts said. He added that, under the guise of patriotism and love of one's country, what often actually takes place is hostility toward minority groups and the seeking of conflict. This happens both in the media and in public spaces.

"It all starts online and quite soon moves into public spaces, for example through the distribution of stickers and other propaganda materials," Preinvalts said.

Democracies encourage civic activism regardless of age, he said, adding that a radical worldview and strongly defined views of the surrounding world are often part of a young person's development.

"Many grow out of it and pose no threat," Preinvalts added.

Glorification of violence

Radicalization becomes a problem when it is accompanied by the glorification of violence or, in the worst-case scenario, its use. Preinvalts said ideological influence has never been as accessible to young people as it is today.

"Content is often determined by algorithms, and after stumbling upon something a few times, a person may unknowingly become a consumer of material that gradually normalizes unlawful behavior," he explained.

"However, it is important to understand that thoughts and beliefs play an important role in maintaining democracy. We have a free society," the official continued.

Preinvalts added that the state cannot and does not want to interfere with people's beliefs, but it has a responsibility is to ensure the safety and security of all residents.

Ministry wants to stop repeat offenders

The Ministry of Justice is now looking for a service provider to help young people with extremist views avoid further offenses and return to education or the labor market. The ministry has announced a small-scale procurement with an estimated value of €40,000.

The service is aimed at young people aged 14 to 29 whose offenses are linked to extremist views or an interest in them. The goal is to reduce the risk of further similar offenses and support young people in distancing themselves from extremist views, developing social skills and reintegrating into society.

The counselor providing the service must have at least two years of experience working with young people or young people exhibiting risky behavior. They must also have knowledge of how extremist views and radicalization develop, including young people's need for belonging, identity crises and the spread of extremist ideologies online.

World.title: Estonia planning to send 'substantial number of locomotives' to Ukraine
World.content:
Estonia is planning to send a "substantial number" of locomotives to Ukraine to help replace those destroyed by Russia, Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) has said.

Tsahkna held a telephone call with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha last week and discussed the current situation in Ukraine, Russia's attacks, and the need for assistance this upcoming winter.

He said Ukraine must receive even "more extensive" practical assistance in the coming months.

"As Russia has targeted critical infrastructure, including the transport network, and has already destroyed or damaged 340 railway carriages this year, we are working to send a substantial number of locomotives to Ukraine. This will help keep the country's transport links operational even under the most difficult conditions," Tsahkna said.

No additional details were given in the press release.

However, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs told ERR's Russian portal on Thursday over 60 locomotives have been identified that could potentially be sent to Ukraine.

The ministry said a Ukrainian Railways expert group visited Estonia earlier this month to assess how the locomotives meet the needs of the Ukrainian railway. The Estonian side is awaiting the experts' response, after which it will continue to seek funding through international mechanisms.

Estonia will also provide Ukraine with an additional €10 million through NATO's PURL initiative, bringing the country's total contribution to €30 million.

Tsahkna also outlined the current situation in Ukraine: "In recent weeks, drone and missile attacks, along with power cuts affecting hundreds of thousands of people, have become part of everyday life in Ukraine. The number of civilian casualties rose by 85 percent in September, and more than 2,000 energy infrastructure facilities have been attacked since July. The conditions for serious peace negotiations will not exist until Russia changes its behaviour."

World.title: EKA graphic design students look 'beyond the veil' in new exhibition
World.content:
An exhibition by graphic design students inspired by an archive hidden in the basement of the Estonian Academy of Arts (EKA) library opened at the university's Billboard Gallery on Friday.

"Who is haunting the school walls, lurking beyond the veil? Hidden in the basement of the EKA library lies an archive of ghosts and restless spirits who are asking to be released. Using the archive as a starting point, the graphic design students have developed an exhibition for the EKA Billboard Gallery, which also became a publication and, finally, an exorcism. This, of course, meant that all working materials were haunted: everything was spooky," a press release says, explaining the exhibition.

Andrew Kuus-Hill, the curator of the exhibition, described the process: "We have enchanted 250 A3-sized prints, pasted them on the billboard, and with the phantoms by our side, performed an exorcism to set them free. Sorcerer hats will be provided on site."

The exhibition "Beyond the Veil" is open at the EKA Billboard Gallery on Kotzebue tänav in Tallinn until December 24.

World.title: Defense minister: Light fighter jets could be procured within 4 years
World.content:
Minister of Defense Martin Herem has said Estonia could need around a dozen light fighter jets to counter jet-powered attack drones, and a procurement could take up to four years.

The Baltic air forces do not have a single fighter jet between them, and NATO's Air Defense Mission monitors the region's skies instead.

Fighter jets cost between €15 million and €100 million each, and while Estonia has wanted them for years, funding has been an obstacle.

For the last 15 years, the Estonian Air Force has used two Czech L-39 light fighter jets for training. But now Herem believes aircraft capable of intercepting jet-powered drones are needed.

"The Ukrainians use F-16 fighter jets to destroy nearly half of them. But we certainly could not afford to go down that route. However, smaller jet-powered aircraft could fulfill that role, whether manned or unmanned," he said.

Minister of Defense Martin Herem. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"Today we know that manned aircraft definitely work. We still do not know very much about unmanned aircraft," the defense minister added.

Light fighter jets would also have a role in hunting loitering munitions, former Air Force commander Vello Loemaa said.

"These aircraft need to be used against drones with speeds ranging from just over 100 to 600 kilometers per hour. The rest of the process – everything involved in engaging a drone, from detection to destruction – is exactly the same as with larger fighter aircraft," he said.

Estonia has pilots for light fighter jets, but they have not been trained to engage aerial targets. "We have the expertise needed to provide further training. But we lack expertise in the specific field of engaging aerial targets," Loemaa said.

A squadron would consist of around a dozen fighter jets, and training would take a year or two.

Vello Loemaa. Source: ERR

Herem believes the aircraft could be procured within four years or even sooner.

"Where and when exactly we will procure them is still quite unclear at the moment. The same goes for where they will be based. But there are certain tasks for which we have no other good alternative," the minister said.

The air force has planned to acquire fighter jets for decades, but its ability to lobby has been weak.

"I would also say there has been a lack of expertise. What is happening now in the war in the skies over Ukraine could have been foreseen. But better late than never, now that this knowledge is reaching others as well," Loemaa said.

He noted that cooperation between the Baltic navies once gave rise to BALTRON, while the air forces also discussed Baltwing, a joint air squadron. However, a lack of resources and common plans has been an obstacle.

World.title: Tallinn Zoo hosts annual Pumpkin Party
World.content:
Although Halloween is still a week away, the pumpkin-loving residents of Tallinn Zoo were presented with more than four tons of donated vegetables for their annual party this weekend.

The zoo's traditional Pumpkin Party took place on Saturday, with the residents being treated to carrots, beetroots, apples, turnips, potatoes, and cabbage alongside the seasonal gourds.

The elephants were one of the most popular attractions, and they were happy to demonstrate their pumpkin-handling skills to the crowds of excited children.

"They love pumpkins the most. The elephant eats the largest quantity of pumpkins – 600 kilograms a year," said Anita Tamm, a communications specialist at Tallinn Zoo.

"Many other animals at the zoo eat them too. The pygmy marmoset eats the least pumpkin at the zoo – just 120 grams a year. Other enthusiasts include hoofed animals, rhinos, apes and monkeys, and reptiles," Tamm said.

The only animals that do not like gourds are carnivores, such as the big cats.

The pumpkin party marks the end of the zoo's vegetable collection campaign. However, anyone can still bring their garden produce to the donation box at the zoo's north gate.

Tallinn Zoo's Pumpkin Party. Source: ERR

World.title: Police tackle underage drinking, illegal scooters in Tartu
World.content:
Police are cracking down on banned electric scooters and minors disturbing public order in Estonia's second-biggest city, Tartu, and carried out one of their largest recent operations targeting young people on Friday.

People out and about in Tartu in southern Estonia late on Friday night may have encountered an unusually large police presence.

Dozens of law enforcement officers were focused on light electric vehicle compliance in the Annelinn and Ülenurme areas. They identified two prohibited scooters, which can travel faster than the legal limit, and two cases of people riding two to a single electric scooter.

Officers also monitored helmet use and spoke with young people.

Kristo Kooskora, a senior inspector at the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA), said that the weather had worked against them this time.

"It rained to some extent throughout the evening, and we saw very few scooters, but that does not mean the problem has disappeared. Various scooter gatherings have also become popular recently, and we have been dealing with those as well. Our work in this area is not over," she told ERR's evening news show "Aktuaalne kaamera."

There was more activity in the city center after midnight.

Nearly 50 police officers patrolled Küüni tänav, which leads from Kaubamaja shopping center to the main square, in an unprecedented operation.

"The checks were conducted by officers simply moving in from both ends and checking everyone caught between the police teams until the officers eventually met in the middle," Kooskora said.

According to preliminary information, police identified nearly 30 intoxicated minors, including some who were severely intoxicated. There were also minors using e-cigarettes and cases involving suspected drug use.

Handcuffs had to be used in several cases because the young people became aggressive. Some also attempted to flee, but their attempts were unsuccessful.

Officers said the operation confirmed the problem with minors is serious. Checks should be carried out more frequently, including on weekdays.

World.title: Justice chancellor: Wild boar cannot be made to suffer when training hunting dogs
World.content:
The Ministry of Regional Affairs and the Ministry of Climate should establish clear legal rules for training hunting dogs using live wild boars to ensure animal welfare and legal clarity, the Chancellor of Justice's Office says.

Four years ago in May, the regional affairs minister issued a regulation on measures to prevent and control African swine fever, introducing an exemption under which the ban on keeping pigs outdoors does not apply to wild boars kept for training hunting dogs.

The Estonian Union for the Protection of Animals asked the chancellor of justice to examine whether the regulation complies with the Animal Protection Act. The organization also pointed out that the law provides no legal basis for using wild boars kept in artificial environments to train hunting dogs and that no detailed requirements have been established for such training.

Deputy Chancellor of Justice-Adviser Olari Koppel said the ban on keeping pigs outdoors is a biosecurity measure and that the minister has the authority to introduce exemptions, provided they comply with EU law and do not undermine animal disease prevention. Koppel therefore sees no reason to believe that the exemption for training hunting dogs violates these conditions.

However, he noted that the regulation only provides an exemption from the ban on keeping pigs outdoors. It does not provide a legal basis for using wild boars to train hunting dogs or authorize activities prohibited under the Animal Protection Act.

"The absence of a specific legal provision does not, however, mean that such an activity is prohibited, provided other applicable rules are followed," Koppel said, adding that it must be possible to conduct training without endangering the animal's welfare.

The law does not establish a specific legal basis or detailed requirements for training hunting dogs using live wild boars. The activity is primarily governed by the Nature Conservation Act and the general animal welfare requirements arising from it.

Under the Animal Protection Act, animals must not be subjected to suffering or pain. According to Koppel, if hunting dog training cannot be conducted without causing such harm, the executive branch cannot make the activity permissible through regulations, guidelines or administrative practices.

"In that case, only the Riigikogu can decide through legislation whether the objective of the training and the benefits it provides justify making an exception to the prohibition established by law," Koppel said.

Koppel said the lack of clarity in the regulations is a problem. To address it, the Ministry of Regional Affairs and the Ministry of Climate should establish the conditions for training hunting dogs in legislation rather than merely in guidelines or explanatory memorandums. This would ensure compliance with animal welfare requirements and provide legal clarity.

World.title: Isamaa party promises to close the climate ministry and create scandals committee
World.content:
Isamaa leader Urmas Reinsalu said at the party's council meeting in Tallinn that the campaign for Estonia's parliamentary elections has begun and is intensifying.

"Those same three parties that, under SALK's leadership, have established a politics of lies under both Kaja Kallas' and Kristen Michal's governments are now maneuvering to escape political punishment and put up camouflage nets," Reinsalu said, referring to the coalition Reform Party and Eesti 200, as well as the opposition Social Democrats.

According to the Isamaa chairman, Eesti 200 is being pressured to withdraw from the elections so that its remaining voters will instead bolster the Reform Party and the Social Democrats.

"So much for political accountability," Reinsalu said. "With the prime minister's speech to the party council, the Reform Party has launched a new wave of fearmongering and lies. This is being dressed up in a marketing campaign whose underlying message is that, yes, we have failed, but we will do better in the future."

"The Reform Party is featuring a beloved actor in its campaign, while the Social Democrats have adopted a different tactic, attempting to conceal their complicity in the Kallas-Michal government by maneuvering to put forward the secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs as their candidate for prime minister. This maneuver will not succeed!" the Isamaa chairman said.

Reinsalu summed up Isamaa's political plans following the 2027 Riigikogu elections with the words "Let the citizens decide."

The party plans to give citizens the right to initiate early elections, following the Latvian model, and to establish a commission of inquiry into scandals after the elections. Lying before the commission would be a criminal offense.

In the area of defense, the party plans to close the border with Russia.

Isamaa also pledged to introduce a supplementary budget that would cut spending.

"Cost-cutting starts at the top: parliamentary and ministerial salaries, closing the Ministry of Climate and a critical review of foundations and subsidies," the party pledged.

On taxes, Isamaa promised to abolish the motor vehicle tax and reduce value-added tax on basic foodstuffs (meat, fish, milk, fruit, vegetables and bread) to 13 percent starting July 1, 2027.

The party also promised to end what it described as the harassment of businesses. "The Climate Act will be thrown in the trash. Investment certainty and a stable operating environment will be restored for the resource-based economy."

The party pledged to carry out an artificial intelligence revolution with the same boldness that Estonia once demonstrated in building its digital state. "The goal is genuine productivity growth, exports and simpler government operations. Sovereignty risks will be taken into account."

Isamaa promised to protect fundamental freedoms and repeal unnecessary restrictions.

The party also pledged to ease the burden of raising children on families and protect teachers' incomes.

In the energy sector, the party will emphasize oil shale. "The energy sector will be provided with dispatchable generation capacity, domestic resources (including oil shale) and affordable prices. Efforts to render oil shale-based energy production unviable will be halted."

The party also promised stricter requirements for the use of Estonian in public spaces, a conservative immigration policy and the restoration of regional balance.

Parliamentary elections will take place in March 2027.

World.title: Iraq, US discuss prospects to strengthen joint cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Defense Nayef al-Shammari and Chargé d’Affaires at the US Embassy in Baghdad Steven Fagin discussed approaches to strengthen cooperation between Baghdad and Washington on Sunday.

During their meeting in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, the two sides discussed bilateral ties and strategies to enhance cooperation between the two countries, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The meeting took place after the US-led international coalition formally completed its full withdrawal and ended Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq on September 30, 2026.

Operation Inherent Resolve—the multinational military campaign formed in 2014 to fight ISIS—officially wrapped up after a 12-year presence.

The end of the combat mission shifts the relationship to a bilateral framework focused on non-combat intelligence sharing, targeted training, and security cooperation rather than active foreign military bases.

Iraqi security forces have assumed full operational control, and the government has set goals to bring remaining armed factions under state regulation.

World.title: Drone attack targets Iranian Kurdish base in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A drone attack carried out by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted on Saturday evening a base belonging to an Iranian Kurdish opposition group in the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

According to reports, the strike hit the headquarters and a guard post of the Komala party. The base is located in the Alana Valley within the Balisan region, northeast of Erbil.

Local security and party officials confirmed the strike caused material damage to buildings but resulted in no casualties.

This attack is a part of Tehran’s intensified campaign against Iraqi-based Iranian Kurdish opposition groups.

Since the military conflict broke out in the region on February 28, Iran has launched over 1,000 drones and missiles into Iraqi Kurdistan, claiming that these groups are directly endangering its national security and have Israeli support.

In mid-August, two explosive-laden drones launched from Iranian territory targeted Iraqi Kurdistan Prime Minister Masrour Barzani’s private office and the home of a top intelligence official.

The strikes took place in Erbil province’s Pirmam area, which is around 30 kilometers north of the capital.

Security personnel recognized the drone as an Iranian-designed “Hadid-110” kamikaze drone carrying explosive payloads.

While Tehran and Iran-backed armed groups have previously accused Iraqi Kurdistan of hosting hostile Iranian Kurdish opposition groups, the authorities in the Kurdistan region of Iraq have always denied using their territory to threaten neighboring nations.

World.title: Iraq, KBR discuss oil sector development
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister for Energy Affairs Mohsen al-Mandalawi and a delegation from US-based KBR discussed on Thursday developing the country’s oil and gas sectors.

KBR’s delegation headed by the company’s president for sustainable technology solutions, Jay Ibrahim, discussed prospects for joint cooperation in the oil, gas, and energy sectors, as well as leveraging the firm’s expertise to develop infrastructure and enhance the efficiency of strategic projects, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The meeting addressed the recovery of associated gas, the development of oil fields, the enhancement of production efficiency, and the modernization of oil facilities.

The two sides also discussed leveraging KBR’s cutting-edge technology solutions to help Iraq’s oil industry grow and to make it easier to carry out key projects that meet requirements for effectiveness, quality, and financial sustainability.

The Iraqi official stressed the importance of ongoing coordination among Iraqi authorities to identify potential areas for collaboration.

Al-Mandalawi noted that the government aims to develop actionable programs related to the Majnoon oil field, the recovery of associated gas at the West Qurna field, initiatives for ammonia production, and efforts to reduce gas flaring at oil fields.

World.title: Iraq sells 10 million barrels of oil at discounts up to $28
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq recently sold 10 million barrels of oil via its southern ports at a discount ranging from $25 to $28 per barrel.

Sources told Attaqa News that most of these shipments were acquired by Indian companies and that the loading took place at the southern ports a few days ago.

Iraq has been unable to sell any oil at a price higher than $100 per barrel since the outbreak of the military conflict in the Middle East, according to two more sources, even though world prices have risen to almost $117 per barrel.

A source at the State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) said that Iraq has not been able to sell oil for more than $85 per barrel.

About a month ago, the company sold some shipments of light crude at around $90 per barrel.

The spokesperson for the Ministry of Oil, Salim al-Rikabi, said that oil sales are still being conducted via the southern ports, and there are variable discounts in place to cover transportation and insurance costs for the purchasing companies.

Recently, Iraq’s average oil exports have risen to approximately 3.2 million barrels per day, according to statements made by Oil Minister Basim Khudair to the official news agency.

Oil shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz account for roughly 3 million barrels per day.

Due to its inadequate tanker fleet, Iraq has resorted to giving substantial discounts on its oil since the start of the conflict in the region, often as much as $32 per barrel.

World.title: Iraq sells 10 million barrels of crude at steep discounts
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq recently sold approximately 10 million barrels of crude oil via its southern export terminals at steep discounts ranging between $25 and $28 per barrel against prevailing international benchmarks, according to industry sources cited by the energy platform Attaqa on Sunday, October 25, 2026.

Trade sources confirmed that Indian refining companies secured the bulk of the discounted shipments, which were loaded at southern offshore terminals in recent days.

Market participants highlighted that Baghdad has been unable to market its crude above $100 per barrel since the outbreak of regional hostilities involving Iran, even as international oil benchmarks surged toward $117 per barrel during recent trading sessions amid maritime risk and escalating conflict dynamics.

Confirming the pricing constraints, an official source at the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) disclosed that recent spot transactions have struggled to clear above $85 per barrel.

The source noted that approximately one month prior, SOMO managed to offload select Basrah Light cargoes at around $90 per barrel before market pressures widened discount spreads. The steep price differentials emerge as the economic observatory “Eco Iraq” reported on Saturday that Iraq’s aggregate crude oil export revenues totaled $37.39 billion from shipments of 533.46 million barrels across the first nine months of 2026.

World.title: Iraq increases port capacity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport has announced that the country’s ports can now handle twice as much cargo as they could in the past.

The ministry’s media director, Hussein Ahmed, said on Sunday that the current capacity of Iraqi ports exceeds 79 million tons of cargo and more than 3.6 million containers.

Ahmed noted that Iraqi ports can now handle twice the cargo volume previously recorded, which was over 40 million tons, as reported by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The Iraqi official mentioned that improvements have been made to the ports, including the construction of new roads, upgrades to existing streets leading to the ports, and the establishment of marshaling yards to alleviate internal congestion.

Iraq’s State Company for Maritime Transport (SCMT), a government-owned maritime company operating under the Iraqi Ministry of Transport, announced on Sunday the reactivation of the Iraqi Line, marked by the arrival of the vessel Basra at the port of Umm Qasr.

SCMT’s director Ahmed Jassim said that the vessel arrived at the port of Umm Qasr carrying containers from the port of Jebel Ali in the United Arab Emirates, signaling the reactivation of the maritime route and the resumption of its commercial voyages after a hiatus that lasted for decades.

World.title: Iraq advances Japanese loan port projects as Grand Faw reach 98%
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Transport is moving to activate two major maritime infrastructure projects—a new floating dock and an integrated shipyards city—financed under the Japanese official development assistance (ODA) loan framework.

The initiative is aimed at expanding vessel repair, maintenance, and auxiliary maritime services across Iraqi ports, coinciding with significant construction milestones at the strategic Grand Faw Port in Basra.

According to statements delivered to the official newspaper by Hussein Ahmed, Director of Media and Government Communications at the Ministry of Transport, ministry officials held technical consultations with representatives of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) loan authority.

The discussions centered on selecting construction locations and addressing civil and logistical engineering requirements for both the floating dry dock and the specialized shipyard zone to modernize national maritime support capabilities.

The operational expansion coincides with near-completion across primary infrastructure phases at the Grand Faw Port. General Director of the General Company for Ports of Iraq (GCPI), Abdullah Aati Abdullah, announced that the port’s core breakwater works have reached 100% completion.

Additionally, the submerged immersed tunnel connecting the port to Umm Qasr has achieved a 98% execution rate, while foundational infrastructure across the facility stands at 94%.

Speaking at a press conference, Abdullah stated that technical teams are preparing to transition toward superstructure and terminal installation phases under the oversight of Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Transport Minister Wahab Al-Hasani.

Abdullah confirmed that preliminary operational trials are scheduled to commence in the upcoming period. He noted that while broader regional shipping traffic has felt the ripple effects of security dynamics around the Strait of Hormuz, work remains focused on expanding container handling capacity, securing yard storage, and cementing Grand Faw’s position as a regional logistics hub connecting the Gulf to Europe.

World.title: Iraq to construct six dams with Turkey and 13 rainwater harvesting barriers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Water Resources revealed plans on Sunday, October 25, 2026, to construct six new dams under the bilateral framework agreement with Turkey, while advancing technical designs and assessments for 13 additional rainwater and seasonal flood harvesting barriers across several governorates to bolster strategic water reserves, support agriculture, and combat desertification.

According to statements delivered to the official newspaper by Ministry Spokesperson and Director General of the General Authority for Irrigation and Reclamation Projects, Khaled Shamal, technical blueprints have been finalized for three dams under the first package of the Turkish framework agreement, preparing them for on-ground execution by Turkish contractors.

The three initial structures comprise the Kharaz Dam in Al-Muthanna Governorate, the Al-Abyad Dam in Ain Al-Tamr in Karbala Governorate, and the Abu Takiya Dam in Nineveh Governorate, with site evaluations underway for an additional three dams proposed under a secondary implementation package.

In parallel with the Turkish cooperation framework, Shamal detailed progress on domestic water harvesting infrastructure designed to capture torrential flash floods and surface runoffs. Technical engineering designs are complete for five submerged check dams in Nineveh Governorate—Sheikh Bakr 1 and 2, Ain Alaq, Ain Ba’shiqa, and Ain Bahzani—with active construction already launched at two sites.

An additional eight water barriers are undergoing hydrologic surveys and final design studies, distributed across Nineveh (3 dams), Najaf (2 dams), Al-Muthanna (2 dams), and Diyala (1 dam), providing vital localized water reserves to support nomadic resettlement, pastoral communities, and regional land reclamation initiatives.

World.title: Delhi Police file FIR against opposition MPs over alleged trespassing at Jamia during student protest
World.content:
Delhi Police have registered an FIR against opposition MPs who visited Jamia Millia Islamia University over alleged trespassing, following a complaint by the university authorities, amid ongoing student protests demanding the restoration of the students' union.

According to news agency ANI, the FIR was registered following the MPs' visit to the campus to meet students protesting for the restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students' Union (JMISU), withdrawal of disciplinary action against protesters and other demands.

Jamia Registrar Md Mahtab Alam Rizvi had accused Congress MPs Imran Masood and Imran Pratapgarhi of entering the campus without authorisation. Rizvi alleged that Masood crossed a wall to enter the premises, while Pratapgarhi broke a lock.

The protest began on October 12, with students demanding the restoration of the students' union and a definite schedule for elections. They have also sought the withdrawal of disciplinary action against students who participated in the agitation.

According to the Press Trust of India (PTI), Jamia's last students' union elections were held in 2005, and the union was dissolved in 2006. The current agitation has also brought attention to student concerns over attendance policies, hostel facilities, scholarships and research stipends.





The protests have drawn support from opposition leaders. PTI reported that Samajwadi Party MP Mohibbullah Nadvi was detained while travelling to meet the protesting students and was later released. Congress MP Imran Masood was also detained near the university during the agitation.

The university administration has said a committee is preparing a draft constitution for the students' union. Registrar Rizvi told ANI that the election schedule would be announced after the draft constitution was submitted.

The administration has also said disciplinary cases against students would be reviewed.

The controversy has widened following reports of graffiti on campus walls, including the slogan âFree Kashmirâ. The university condemned the graffiti, while Masood told ANI that he had denounced the slogan and maintained that Kashmir is an integral part of India.

The FIR marks a further escalation in the standoff between the university administration, protesting students and opposition politicians.

World.title: Women founders are building India's social startups, their representation in nonprofits outpaces corporate leadership by a big margin, shows study
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A survey of more than 145 organisations working in the social impact space shows that over 57% of non-profits have at least one female founder â more than three times the 18% share reported among Indian startups.

Moreover, female representation in the nonprofit sector outpaces corporate leadership, where women hold just 1.8% of CEO positions, 4.4% of CFO positions, and 29% of executive director roles.

These findings are part of accelerator for non-profits Change Engineâs âEast of Doing Goodâ report - âAccess to flexible funding: a Gender Lensâ. The survey covers small organisations (annual budgets less than Rs 1 crore), medium (annual budgets between Rs 1 crore -5 crore) and large organisations (Rs 5 crore and more).

The study sample also had an almost equal split between organisations eligible for foreign funding (with FCRA or US 501(c)) and those that were not.

Out of the 145 plus organisations surveyed, nearly 31% have only female founders, while around 27% have both male and female founders.

The research also shows that women are not only founding more nonprofits, but women founded organisations are better funded and hold more long term flexible funding.





The study found that non-profits with atleast one female founder also had bigger budgets. The data shows that 70% of organisations with at least one female founder have an annual budget of over Rs 1 crore, compared to 43.5% of organisations with only-male founders.

Also around 21% of organisations with at least one female founder have more than 25% of their budget in flexible unrestricted funding, compared to just about 13% of organisations with only male founders.

Flexible funding is the non-programmatic funding that nonprofits can use to invest in talent, technology, research and strengthening the organisation.

As far as long-term grants are concerned it turns out that over 65% of organisations with at least one female founder have access to multi-year funding (three years or more), compared to around 56% of organisations with only male founders. Among these, around 27% of organisations with at least one female founder have received multi-year grants above Rs 1 crore, compared to just about 11% of only male founder organisations.

The report highlights that when asked to rate (on a scale of 1-5) how easy it was to raise unrestricted funds from corporate social responsibility (CSR), high net-worth individuals (HNIs), domestic foundations, foreign foundations, and crowdfunding/retail, organisations with at least one female founder scored consistently scored higher across every category with an average score of 2.41 in comparison with 2.06 of organisations with only male founders.

However, challenges remain. The study shows that cheque sizes remain small for everyone: âA staggering 82% of organisations with at least one female founder and 83% of only male founded organisations said typical unrestricted cheque sizes in India are less than Rs 25 lakh, showing that the small-cheque problem cuts across gender lines,â the study highlights.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Varun Aggarwal and Shubham Bansal, co-founders, Change Engine highlighted that the findings show that women are leading Indiaâs social sector and building bigger and better resourced organisations.

We need to encourage more women to come into this sector," Aggarwal asserted. âIn our accelerator, we meet women founders who are building strong, ambitious institutions to tackle some of Indiaâs biggest social challenges.

Itâs encouraging to see that what weâve been observing on the ground is now backed by data. Six in ten nonprofits in our survey were founded by a woman founder,â Bansal added.

However, the Change Engine founders highlight that the access to unrestricted flexible funding remains consistently low across the board with 80% of the surveyed founders reporting that they struggle to scale their work due to the lack of unrestricted funding. âThis funding rigidity forces organisations to spend disproportionate time on fundraising, rather than focusing on innovation and impact,â they added.

World.title: 'Pakistan has no right': Congress distances itself from ally Farooq Abdullah's Kashmiri remark
World.content:
J&K Congress distances itself from Farooq Abdullah's Pakistan remarks; Kashmiri Pandit groups seek FIR

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

What Farooq Abdullah said

NEW DELHI: The Jammu and Kashmir Congress has distanced itself from National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullahâs remarks that Pakistan was helping Kashmiris by keeping the Kashmir issue alive at international fora.âThe Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Congress Committee has distanced itself from the statement of NC president Farooq Abdullah and asserted that Pakistan has no right to talk about or interfere in our internal affairs as J&K is an integral part of India,â J&K Congress chief spokesperson Ravinder Sharma said in a post on X.However, speaking to reporters, Sharma said Abdullahâs remarks appeared to reflect frustration over the Centreâs failure to fulfil its promise to restore statehood to Jammu and Kashmir.âPakistan has consistently waged a proxy war against India and caused the deaths of innocent people in J&K by sponsoring terrorism. Pakistanâs role in promoting terrorism must be condemned, and strict action should continue against it,â Sharma said, reiterating that the Congress was firmly opposed to any interference by Pakistan in Indiaâs internal affairs.Sharma said Abdullah should clarify the intent behind his remarks, adding that opposition to Pakistan-sponsored terrorism and the demand for restoration of statehood were separate but equally important issues.He also suggested that Abdullahâs comments were directed at what he described as discrimination against minorities across the country and the policies pursued by BJP governments in various states.âThe remarks reflected resentment against a pattern of oppression and discrimination,â the Congress leader said.Sharma further said Jammu and Kashmir continued to face resentment over the delay in restoring statehood, despite repeated assurances by the Centre before the Supreme Court, Parliament and the public.Meanwhile, some Kashmiri Pandit groups have filed a police complaint seeking an FIR against the former chief minister over his comments.His remarks drew criticism from some Kashmiri Pandit groups, which lodged a police complaint seeking the registration of an FIR against the former chief minister.Meanwhile, Kashmiri Pandit groups Panun Kashmir and the Jammu State People's Movement (JSPM) have lodged a police complaint at the Channi police station in Jammu, seeking the registration of an FIR against Abdullah over his remarks.The complaint, submitted by Panun Kashmir chairman Tito Ganju and JSPM chairman Col Ajay Raina (retd), sought an investigation into statements attributed to Abdullah concerning the constitutional status of Jammu and Kashmir and alleged religious polarisation.It cited his reported remarks questioning the prospects of justice from the Union government and warning that the people of J&K risked losing their identity if they failed to confront the prevailing political circumstances.The complainants also referred to remarks attributed to Abdullah about the demolition of mosques, homes and shops, as well as his assertion that Hindus and Muslims were being pitted against each other. They urged the police to examine the statements in their entirety, taking into account their context, the audience addressed and their potential implications.The complaint sought an FIR under Sections 152, 196 and 197 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with any other provisions that may apply based on the investigation.The provisions cited concern acts endangering India's sovereignty, unity and integrity, promoting enmity between groups, and certain imputations or assertions prejudicial to national integration, a Panun Kashmir spokesperson said.BJP leader Jahanzaib Sirwal also criticised Abdullah, accusing him of double standards for invoking Pakistan to question India's intentions while overlooking the suffering of people across the Line of Control.âIt was deeply unfortunate that a leader who has dominated J&Kâs political landscape for decades continues to rely on the Pakistan narrative rather than account for the consequences of his own politics.âFarooq Sahib has spent decades building a political narrative around Pakistan, but has he ever honestly answered what this politics has delivered to the people of J&K?âHis party does not have to seek votes in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, but that cannot be an excuse to remain silent on the atrocities and sufferings of the people living there. Human rights cannot be selective, and political morality cannot change with electoral convenience,â Sirwal said.He added that the NC leadership must stop treating Pakistan as a convenient political instrument to invoke whenever it suited its narrative.Addressing a party event in Baramulla on Saturday, Abdullah questioned whether people in Jammu and Kashmir could expect justice from the Centre.âWhat hope will you (people of J&K) have from them (Delhi)? Will you expect that they will do justice for you?" he said.Urging Kashmiris to remain courageous in confronting Delhi, Abdullah warned that their identity could disappear if they failed to do so.âIf not, you will be erased. Even our trace and identity will disappear. They are silent today because there is noise in the world, and our neighbour is constantly behind this. Everywhere they say, 'the decision regarding Kashmir has not been made'. That is what is saving us. Otherwise, their intentions are not good,â he said.

World.title: PM Modi inaugurates RBI's Rs 169-crore data centre, cybersecurity institute in Odisha
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) Rs 169-crore data centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute at Info Valley-II in Jatni, near Bhubaneswar, Odisha.

Spread across 18.55 acres, the facility's foundation stone was laid by then RBI governor Shaktikanta Das on March 22, 2023. The data centre will host mission-critical payment and settlement systems, along with other key RBI initiatives, according to a government statement.

It is expected to improve the reach, efficiency and reliability of digital financial services while providing a secure foundation for India's increasingly technology-driven financial sector.

The Cybersecurity Training Institute will focus on training, research and capacity building in cybersecurity and enterprise technology, helping strengthen capabilities across the financial sector.

The location was chosen for its geographical stability, away from seismically active zones and high-risk international border areas, officials said according to news agency PTI. This is expected to reduce the facility's exposure to natural disasters and geopolitical vulnerabilities.

The facilities have been designed to provide a secure, resilient, scalable and future-ready computing ecosystem for the RBI and the wider financial sector.

Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra, Odisha Governor Brajmohan Ram, chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi and other senior leaders were also present at the inauguration.

World.title: Indian American physician Navin Shah commits $525,000 to infectious disease program in Pune
World.content:
The five-year initiative, established in collaboration with

Johns Hopkins University

, will support research, medical training, faculty exchanges and patient care at BJ Government Medical College.

Indian American physician and philanthropist Dr. Navin C. Shah has committed $525,000 to establish an infectious disease program at his alma mater, BJ Government Medical College in Pune, Maharashtra, in collaboration with Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore.

The five-year initiative, named the Navin C. Shah Infectious Disease Program, will support research, medical education, faculty and student exchanges, and patient care, particularly benefiting underserved communities in Pune.

The agreement was signed at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, with Shah and Dr. Amita Gupta, the Florence Sabin Professor of Infectious Diseases and director of the Division of Infectious Diseases at the Johns Hopkins School of Medicine, participating in the ceremony.

Gupta, who is also the founder and faculty co-chair of the Johns Hopkins India Institute, has been involved in infectious disease research and medical collaborations in India for more than two decades.

The initiative represents a significant philanthropic investment in a longstanding academic partnership between Johns Hopkins and BJ Government Medical College, one of Puneâs major public medical institutions.





âThe purpose is to help my medical school in training, education, research and patient care as far as ID (infectious diseases) is concerned,â Shah, a resident of Potomac, MD, told The American Bazaar after the signing ceremony.

For Shah, who grew up in Pune and graduated from BJ Government Medical College, the initiative is both a professional commitment and a personal effort to give back to the institution that shaped his medical career.

âI grew up in Pune, so it is a win-win situation for me because not only my medical college will be benefited in the training, education, research and patient care, but other people, other hospitals which are treating poor patients in Pune will be benefited,â he said.

Expanding research and patient care

The new program will focus on infectious diseases that continue to pose major public health challenges in India, including tuberculosis, HIV and infections resistant to commonly used antibiotics.

In an interview with The American Bazaar, Gupta said Johns Hopkins researchers have been working with BJ Government Medical College since 2003 on a broad range of infectious disease projects.

âThe work that we do includes right from research to new treatments for TB, for HIV, for highly drug-resistant infections in adults and in children and pregnant women,â she said.

The collaboration also encompasses medical education, training for doctors and nurses, and exchanges involving students and faculty from Johns Hopkins and institutions in Pune.

Gupta emphasized the importance of BJ Government Medical Collegeâs role in serving economically disadvantaged patients.

âBJ Medical College is well known for really being the public hospital taking care of the poorest of the poor in Pune,â she said.

The new funding will help expand activities that may not be adequately covered by conventional research grants.

A patient care fund will also be established to support treatment and related needs.

Gupta said the gift would support research, education and patient care over the five-year period, allowing the institutions to pursue additional opportunities beyond their existing projects.

The program is also expected to strengthen the exchange of medical expertise between India and the United States.

According to Shah, the arrangement will include visits by four Johns Hopkins faculty members to India and two BJ Government Medical College faculty members to the United States, along with exchanges involving students and medical residents.

The initiative will also support an annual seminar bringing together medical experts from Pune and elsewhere in India.

Shah said a seminar is scheduled to begin December 4, providing an early opportunity for specialists to share knowledge and discuss advances in infectious disease treatment.

The Maryland urologist noted that the collegeâs affiliated hospital has approximately 1,800 beds and serves large numbers of patients from economically disadvantaged backgrounds.

Decades-long partnership

The new initiative builds on a relationship between Johns Hopkins researchers and Pune-based medical institutions that began with research into preventing HIV transmission from mothers to their children.

During the signing ceremony, Gupta recalled arriving at Johns Hopkins in 2003, attracted in part by the opportunity to work in India.

She credited Dr. Robert Bollinger, a Johns Hopkins physician and researcher, with helping establish early collaborations involving BJ Medical College and Indiaâs National AIDS Research Institute.

One of the initial projects examined the use of nevirapine to reduce mother-to-child HIV transmission.

Over the years, the research partnership expanded considerably.

âWeâre looking at new TB drugs, TB vaccine, diagnostics, taking care of HIV, looking at drug resistant infections,â Gupta said during the ceremony.

She noted that researchers had also studied dengue and health conditions such as diabetes and alcohol misuse that can complicate the treatment of patients with infectious diseases.

Beyond research, Gupta described the partnership as a two-way learning experience for physicians, scientists and students.

She said her work in Pune had allowed Johns Hopkins faculty to learn from Indian colleagues and patients while giving American medical professionals opportunities to participate in collaborative research.

Philanthropic contributions, she explained, provide flexibility that conventional grant funding often lacks.

Such support allows researchers to pursue innovative ideas, expand educational opportunities and strengthen patient services.

âWithout the sort of gratitude and the support of philanthropists such as yourself and your family, you know, much of what we do, we go hand to mouth with our grants,â she told Shah.

The gift, she added, would enable the collaborators to be more creative and innovative in their work.

Gupta also said she planned to travel to Pune for a December 3 inauguration associated with Shahâs contribution.

Johns Hopkins-India connection

The initiative comes as Johns Hopkins continues expanding its academic and research engagement with India through the Johns Hopkins India Institute.

Gupta said the institute was created to bring together researchers and academic programs that had previously operated largely independently across the university.

Its goal is to strengthen collaboration across disciplines and connect Johns Hopkins faculty with Indian universities, hospitals, government agencies and nonprofit organizations.

Among its initiatives are a TB-free schools program, a fellowship supporting young women scientists in India, and collaborative research grants covering areas such as artificial intelligence in healthcare, medical education and public health.

Gupta said Johns Hopkinsâ India-related research and collaborative activities have involved approximately $80 million over the past decade.

The new Pune initiative will become part of this broader network while retaining a specific focus on infectious diseases, medical training and patient care.

Gupta also expressed hope that Shahâs contribution would encourage other alumni of BJ Government Medical College and members of the Indian diaspora to support healthcare and education in India.

âOne of the goals of his gift is to really get other alumni from BJ Medical College or those who care about Pune and more and then throughout India to be able to be generous with their philanthropic giving,â she said.

Giving back to his alma mater

Shah, a founder of the American Association of Physicians of Indian Origin (AAPI), has long been associated with efforts to connect Indian American medical professionals with healthcare initiatives in India.

His latest commitment reflects the continuing role of Indian American physicians in supporting medical education and healthcare institutions in their country of origin.

For Shah, the decision to fund the infectious disease program was driven by his connection to Pune and his belief that international medical partnerships can improve healthcare delivery.

He hopes the program will strengthen the ability of BJ Government Medical College and other Pune hospitals to diagnose, study and treat infectious diseases.

Gupta sees the collaboration in similarly broad terms.

âI always look at it as itâs a bilateral partnership. Truly we learn and we give,â she said.

âThe world is a much better and safer place and a more productive and innovative place if we are working together across our geographies and our disciplines.â

For BJ Government Medical College, the initiative promises additional resources, international expertise and opportunities for medical professionals to participate in research and training.

For Shah, it marks a return to his roots through an investment in the institution where his medical journey began.

âSo education, training, research and patient care,â he said, summarizing his expectations for the program. âHopefully my college, with the help of Hopkins, will improve in ID treatment, infectious disease treatment.â

World.title: BSF apprehends four Pakistani fishermen in Kutch, seizes boat
World.content:
The Border Security Force (BSF) has apprehended four Pakistani fishermen who allegedly entered Indian waters for crab-catching activities and seized a fishing boat near the India-Pakistan border in Gujaratâs Kutch district.

According to news agency PTI, the fishermen were apprehended from the Sir Creek area on Sunday following specific intelligence inputs, an official said. The fishermen were identified as Kadir Thaimor, Muhammad Mussa, Azgar Thaimor and Ahsan Jat, all residents of Chach Jaan Khan village in Pakistanâs Sindh province, according to information provided by the BSF.

Sir Creek is a narrow, marshy tidal channel in the Rann of Kutch, along the coastal region between Gujarat and Pakistanâs Sindh province.

The area is strategically sensitive because the longstanding India-Pakistan boundary dispute over the creek affects the demarcation of the maritime boundary in the Arabian Sea.

The regionâs shallow waters, tidal channels and extensive marshlands make navigation and border surveillance challenging. Fishing activities in the area can also lead to fishermen crossing into the other countryâs waters, prompting apprehensions by security personnel.

World.title: 'Too deferential to govt': Former SC judge questions ex-CJI Chandrachud’s approach to appointments
World.content:
Congress flags judicial independence concerns over claims in ex SC judge's memoir

Congress flags judicial independence concerns

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Is Justice D Y Chandrachud's approach to judicial appointments acceptable in your opinion? Yes, he is doing what's necessary. No, it undermines judicial independence. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Former Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has questioned former Chief Justice of India (CJI) D Y Chandrachud's approach to judicial appointments, alleging that he was "too deferential to the government". He also expressed concern over the practice of discussing candidates with the executive before formal Collegium deliberations.In his forthcoming memoir, Without Fear or Favour, Justice Kaul recounts a Collegium meeting to fill six vacancies in the Supreme Court, during which five names had been agreed upon in advance. He alleges that Justice Chandrachud proposed a sixth candidate at the last minute and considered seeking the government's view on the appointment."The Chief Justice drew me aside into a separate room and wondered aloud whether he should telephone out to check the government's view," Kaul wrote in his book.Speaking to news portal The Wire about his memoir, Kaul said the Collegium must resist executive pressure to safeguard judicial independence.Asked whether Justice Chandrachud was trying to please the government or seeking its prior approval, Kaul said, "I don't think it was a question of pleasing the government, but what had happened was that he had discussed the names with me earlier."We had agreed on five names, and I thought the collegium would be quite okay with the other members of the collegium, and this (sixth) name was propped up at the last minute with me while going to the collegium meeting. I said that name is not acceptable to me and will not be acceptable."He said Justice Chandrachud wanted him to support the additional candidate, but he believed the other Collegium members would also oppose the proposal."And well, he wanted me to collaborate and go ahead with the name. I said even if I do that, the others will not. I believe, and that's what happened in the meeting. I told him this will not get through because I know the views of the other collegiate members. Maybe he had already taken some kind of an approval for the other names, including the sixth name," Kaul said.He expressed concern over the practice of discussing judicial appointments with the government before formal Collegium meetings."So this has become, unfortunately, a practice of names being discussed in some kind of a previous discussion with the government," he told senior journalist Karan Thapar."It has been happening, I think, before and after, which is what troubles me. That's why I have written that when the government introduced the NJAC (the National Judicial Appointments Commission) in 2015, we would at least have sat across the table and discussed it. It could have been fine-tuned. It could be modulated," Kaul said.Justice Kaul, who retired in December 2023, wrote that differences over how to deal with the executive strained his relationship with Justice Chandrachud, under whom he served on the Collegium from June 2022."There is a difference between consultation and what I came to regard as pre-approval, seeking the government's nod before the collegium had even formally deliberated," Kaul wrote in his memoir.Explaining why he considered Justice Chandrachud "too deferential to the government on appointment matters," Kaul said the practice could create difficulties for future Chief Justices, particularly those with shorter tenures."Well, he believed that this is how it had been happening, and I was of the view that you, with a chief justice like you, and with two years' tenure, and with your own merit and the trust, if you do this, the successors would have a problem in not following this practice because they have shorter tenures.""And the government would get used to a particular methodology before appointments to the Supreme Court were made, and that's why I endeavoured to discourage him from discussing everything beforehand," Kaul said.The former judge also raised objections to the transfer of a case concerning the reconsideration of certain aspects of a Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) judgment from a bench headed by him to another bench. He argued that cases should not be reassigned because of apprehensions about how a particular bench might decide them.The Congress on Sunday raised concerns over the independence of the judiciary under the Narendra Modi government, citing revelations in the forthcoming memoir. The party asserted that the institution responsible for upholding the Constitution must remain free from pressure exerted by those in power.Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh shared a media report quoting the pre-publication manuscript of Kaul's memoir, Without Fear of Favour, which reportedly states that Chief Justice of India (CJI) Justice D Y Chandrachud was "too deferential to the Government" on judicial appointments.In a post on X, Ramesh said, "A book by former Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has raised serious questions regarding the independence of the judiciary during the tenure of the Modi government."Ramesh said Kaul had highlighted several concerning incidents, including alleged government interference in judicial appointments, attempts to secure government approval before Collegium meetings and the government's questioning of the caste of a judge belonging to a minority community.He added that issues many had previously been hesitant to discuss openly had now been documented by Kaul in measured and deliberate language."Strikingly, a former Chief Justice of India (CJI) has not denied that discussions with the government take place prior to judicial appointments. When former CJI Justice Chandrachud acknowledges that the government engages with the CJI and plays a role in the appointment process, the concerns surrounding judicial independence become even more profound," Ramesh said.The Congress leader also flagged Kaul's account of an incident involving a case under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). According to Ramesh, Kaul revealed that after a bench presided over by him raised the possibility of reconsidering certain aspects of a court ruling in the case, the matter was reassigned to another bench without consulting him."This points to the extent of the government's day-to-day interference in the functioning of the Supreme Court," Ramesh said.Questioning the implications of the alleged incidents, he said, "When there is pressure to obtain government approval for judicial appointments, and when benches hearing sensitive cases are altered, one must ask -- in the interest of safeguarding democracy -- if this does not constitute pressure on the judiciary and an erosion of its independence, then what does?"Emphasising the importance of judicial independence in a democracy, Ramesh said, "The institution tasked with upholding the Constitution must remain free from the pressures of those in power. In a democracy, the independence of the judiciary is not merely an option; it is an absolute necessity," Ramesh asserted.

World.title: DK Shivakumar's big warning to Bengaluru IT firms over sidelining Kannadiga candidates

NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister

has warned that the state government will take action against IT companies found to be deliberately sidelining Kannadigas in job opportunities.

World.title: Cyber commandos lead Delhi Police’s digital fight amid protests, bomb hoaxes, crypto frauds
World.content:
Amid a series of hoax bomb threats and ongoing youth-led protests demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner over alleged voter list manipulation, Delhi Police’s cyber commandos are working round the clock to trace digital footprints, identify misleading social media content and help investigators unravel complex cybercrime cases. From examining email records and Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) to tracing cryptocurrency transactions in digital arrest scams, the specialised personnel use technical expertise to turn digital clues into investigative leads.

In an exclusive interaction with The Hindu, cyber commando Akhil Raj, who works with the Delhi Police’s Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit, explained how the team tracks suspects, investigates online fraud and flags manipulated videos circulating on social media.

Mr. Raj, who was involved in investigations into hoax bomb threats received in Delhi in 2024 and 2025, said investigators approach email service providers for information such as IP addresses, registered contact numbers, and alternate email IDs. They routinely seek records spanning six months to a year to establish a sender’s online activity.

The process becomes more difficult when suspects use Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) or the Onion Router (Tor) network to conceal their digital footprints. However, in some cases involving free VPN services, a temporary break in the connection can expose the actual IP address, allowing investigators to approach internet service providers for further details.

Of the more than 20 bomb threat cases he has investigated, the police traced the senders in four to five instances, Mr. Raj said. These included three cases in which school students used VPN connections to send hoax emails in an attempt to postpone examinations.

Misleading content

With protests continuing in the Capital, cyber commandos are also monitoring social media for triggering and misleading posts, reels and videos. The team constantly tracks keywords to identify potentially manipulated content.

Once a video is flagged, the police send takedown requests to social media platforms such as X and Meta. Recalling a recent case involving an AI-generated video of Delhi Police Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vivek Bhagat, Mr. Raj said the police identified the video and initiated legal action.

Earlier this month, a 24-year-old ‘independent’ journalist was arrested from Haryana’s Palwal for allegedly circulating the deepfake that ‘falsely’ portrayed the ACP in an objectionable situation with a woman. He was booked under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for tarnishing the image of the police force and attempting to incite public unrest during the CJP protests.

Additional Commissioner of Police (IFSO) Sanjay Bhatia said cyber commandos have improved the speed of investigations by enabling officers to map digital trails and connections more quickly.

“What would earlier take weeks to establish — the path of a crime and the various digital nodes involved — can now be mapped in just two to four days,” he said. “They bring specialised skills that are not available elsewhere in the force, and we are constantly working to upgrade their expertise as technology and cybercrime evolve,” Mr. Bhatia added.

Specialised training

The Cyber Commando programme was inaugurated in 2024, with 300 personnel trained in its first batch. The Union Home Ministry’s Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) selected officers from across States through an entrance examination focused on cybersecurity and cybercrime.

The selected officers underwent six months of residential training at eight centres, including the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) and Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs). Mr. Raj trained at the NFSU in Gandhinagar. He has worked with the Delhi Police’s IFSO unit since 2019 and spent nearly two years as a cyber commando. His areas of expertise include digital forensics, cryptocurrency investigations and malware analysis.

Delhi has eight cyber commandos. Their deployment depends on a case’s technical requirements and the expertise needed. In the event of a ransomware attack on a government system, for instance, the I4C identifies a suitable commando to assist the investigation alongside the State police, which remains the first responder.

Following the money

Cryptocurrency-related fraud, including ‘digital arrest’ scams where stolen amounts are quickly converted into cryptocurrency and transferred abroad, is a growing area of concern.

Investigators seek information from exchanges used to convert cryptocurrency into Indian currency and request customer information that could help identify those behind the transactions. They also examine publicly accessible blockchain records to trace subsequent transfers and establish links between wallets, Mr. Raj said.

Mr. Raj spends much of his working day behind a large screen, analysing digital evidence, correlating records and tracing connections across online platforms and networks. The aim is to turn scattered technical clues into leads that investigators can use to identify suspects and build their cases.

World.title: 19 candidates in fray for VMC Mayor’s post
World.content:
The Vijayawada Municipal Corporation (VMC) on Sunday (October 25, 2026) released the final list of candidates in the fray for the posts of ward members and mayor. According to the list, 19 candidates are in the race for the mayoral post, while 349 are contesting for 86 ward member posts in the ongoing Second Ordinary Elections to Urban Local Bodies, 2026.

While 24 candidates filed nominations for the Mayoral post, the duplicates were rejected, bringing the number down to 19. None of the Mayoral candidates withdrew their nominations.

Jana Sena Party, YSRCP, Aam Aadmi Party, Indian Union Muslim League Party, Bharata Chaitanya Yuvajana Party, Navarang Congress Party, Reforms Party of India each have one candidate in the race to the post of Mayor. The remaining 10 are all Independents.

For the ward member posts, totally 970 nominations were filed from October 16 to 18. Out of these, 474 candidates withdrew their nominations and some others were rejected. Most of the withdrawls were seen among TDP candidates (180), followed by Jana Sena Party (121), YSRCP (97) and BJP (43).

Meanwhile, campaigning is going on at a brisk pace in the city. While there is a tight contest between NDA candidate Vangaveeti Radha Krishna and YSRCP candidate Rayana Bhagyalakshmi, the entry of former IPS officer A.B. Venkateswara Rao as an Independent candidate has offered the voters a new alternative.

On Sunday, while Mr. Venkateswara Rao was campaigning near Machavaram, criticising both YSRCP and TDP for corruption, his political vitriol gave way to a brief episode of affection when he met NDA candidate Mr. Vangaveeti Radha Krishna, who was also campaigning in the opposite direction. The two candidates exchanged a warm embrace as onlookers stood by, clicking pictures of them.

World.title: 15 candidates in fray for Visakhapatnam Mayor’s post
World.content:
A total of 15 candidates are contesting for the post of Mayor in the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) general elections–2026, Mayor Election Returning Officer B. Dayanidhi said in a release on Sunday.

A total of 29 nominations were received for the GVMC Mayor’s post, of which 8 nominations were rejected, while the remaining 21 nominations were found valid. During the withdrawal of nominations on October 21, six candidates withdrew their nominations, he said.

Subsequently, in the notification issued by the Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission on October 22, 2026, it was directed that the final list of candidates contesting for the post of Mayor in the GVMC elections be announced on October 25, 2026. Accordingly, 15 candidates remain in the fray for the Mayor’s post, the Returning Officer stated.

Prominent candidates among them include Mukka Sravani from Telugu Desam Party (TDP), Varudu Kalyani from YSRCP (YSRCP), Devara Naga Sunanda Devi from Indian National Congress (INC), K. Keerthana Grace from Bahujan Samaj Party, and Nammi Bhavani from Bharata Chaitanya Yuvajana Party.

World.title: Man killed in Keralam’s Kochi as luxury car, allegedly driven by judge’s minor son, hits scooter
World.content:
A 55-year-old man was killed after a luxury car, allegedly driven by a 17-year-old boy, rammed the scooter he was riding in the early hours of Sunday (October 25, 2026).

The deceased has been identified as Jayabalakrishnan of Chittur, Cheranalloor. This is the second road accident allegedly involving teenaged drivers in Kochi within a fortnight.

The Cheranalloor police on Sunday recorded the arrest of the minor driver, reportedly the son of a judicial officer. The boy was released on bail from the police station later in the day under Section 8 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, according to the police.

The accident occurred around 2.20 a.m. near a car showroom at Maraparambu on Container Road in Cheranalloor. The boy was travelling alone in the car from Vallarpadam towards Kalamassery when it hit the scooter, which was moving in the same direction, as per the FIR. Cheranalloor Circle Inspector told the media that the boy was not under the influence of alcohol as per preliminary medical examination.

Mr. Jayabalakrishnan, who was returning after shutting his eatery at Chittur, reportedly succumbed to his injuries on the spot.

The police have registered a case against the minor driver on charges of rash driving and rash or negligent act that does not amount to culpable homicide under Sections 281 and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Later in the day, the police added Section 105 of BNS which prescribes the punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder in the FIR. The Section was added amid protests and criticism against the police for releasing the accused on station bail. “Further action based on the fresh charge will be taken against the accused,” a senior police officer said. Relatives of the victim, supported by various political parties, staged protests in front of the Cheranalloor police station after the accused was let out on bail.

The final rites of the victim was held at the Pachalam crematorium on Sunday.

. Mr. Jayabalakrishnan is survived by his wife Manju and three children.

The accident comes days after three youths were killed after an allegedly speeding luxury car driven by a 19-year-old youth rammed the two-wheeler they were riding near Nedumbassery.

Strict action sought

Ernakulam MLA T.J. Vinod, meanwhile, requested Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala to examine if the police’s act of granting station bail to the minor accused was legally correct. He said the responsibility of the car owner who permitted the minor to drive the vehicle should also come under the purview of the investigation. “There shouldn’t be any compromise in the probe on account of the family background and influence of the accused,” he said.

World.title: Nilgiris district hit by 62 minor landslips in a day till October 25 morning
World.content:
The ecologically fragile Nilgiris district in Tamil Nadu was hit by as many as 62 landslips in the 24 hours ending at 7 a.m. on Sunday (October 25, 2026), following light to moderate spell of rain across the district.

According to official data from the district administration, heavy damage to infrastructure was reported, with 15 huts partly damaged, one hut fully collapsed and 16 revetments damaged across the district. The continuous spell led to the damage of two high-tension poles, nine low-tension poles and one distribution transformer. A total of 28 trees were uprooted.

Parsons Valley gets highest rainfall

The district recorded a cumulative total rainfall of 453.9 mm during the 24-hour period, with an overall average rainfall of 14.64 mm. Ten out of the 31 rain gauge statins in the district received moderate rain, with the remaining locations recorded light rain in the 24 hours.

Parsons Valley in Udhagamandalam taluk recorded the highest rainfall in the district at 52 mm, followed by Upper Bhavani in Kundah taluk at 38 mm and Naduvattam and Glenmorgan (also in Udhagamandalam taluk) at 37 mm each.

The district had 19 landslips in the previous 24 hours ending on Saturday (October 24) morning.

Vehicular traffic, tourism

Traffic along Mettupalayam-Coonoor stretch remains suspended and vehicles are being allowed to and fro Nilgiris along Mettupalayam-Kotagiri Road between 7 a.m. and 6 p.m., said police sources.

People who want to travel to Coonoor and Udhagamandalam (Ooty) from Mettupalayam and vice versa must use Kotagiri Road during the permitted hours. Tourism activities in the Nilgiris also remain suspended for three days from Saturday.

Heavy rain on Sunday

Several parts of the Nilgiris received heavy rains from Sunday afternoon and continued through the night. As a result, new landslips were reported on the Coonoor-Mettupalayam ghat section. A man and his son suffered injuries after a tree fell onto their house at Ketti in the district. A huge tree fell onto a stationary car near Rose Garden at Udhagamandalam town, which received heavy rain in the evening. On Avalanche road, a tree fell onto a house. Trees were uprooted at several other locations.

Burliyar landslip site
